There, David asked in awe, “How can the ark of the LORD come into my care?”; here Elizabeth asks, “And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” There, David leaped and danced before the ark; here, “the child leaped in her womb.” There, the ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-edom and brought blessing; here, “Mary remained with her about three months.” Mary is the new Ark, carrying not the tablets of the Law but the Word made flesh.

Elizabeth, “filled with the Holy Spirit,” speaks the words that the Church repeats millions of times a day in the Hail Mary: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” She calls Mary “the mother of my Lord,” the first time in St Luke's Gospel that a human voice calls Jesus Lord, and the basis of the Church's faith that Mary is truly the Mother of God (Catechism 495). And she praises Mary's faith: “blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.” Then Mary sings. The Magnificat is woven out of the Psalms and the song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2), the prayer of a young woman who knew the Scriptures by heart. “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.” She does not boast of herself; she boasts of God, who “has done great things for me.” And then the song widens to the whole of history: God “has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.” The God who chose a poor girl from Nazareth is the God who takes the side of the poor. Every evening, at Vespers, the Church sings this song with Mary. On this last day of May we may ask her for two gifts: her haste to serve, and her joy in God.
conn: “Daughter Zion.”
A poetic title for Jerusalem and the people of God (Zephaniah 3:14; Zechariah 9:9). The Church sees in Mary the true daughter Zion, in whom God comes to dwell (Catechism 722).
“In your midst.”
Hebrew beqirbek, used twice in Zephaniah 3:15, 17; it can also mean “within you,” even “in your womb.” Many scholars hear an echo of it in the angel's greeting to Mary in Luke 1:28–31.
“With haste.”
Greek meta spoudes: with eagerness, with zeal. Mary's haste is not anxiety but the readiness of love. St Ambrose wrote that the grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts (in substance).
The hill country of Judah.
Tradition identifies Elizabeth's town with Ein Karem, about seven kilometres west of Jerusalem, where two churches recall the Visitation and the birth of John.
The new Ark.

Luke's account echoes 2 Samuel 6: the ark goes up to the hill country of Judah, David asks how it can come to him, he leaps before it, and it remains three months. Mary carries the Word of God made flesh (Catechism 2676).
“The child leaped.”
The same verb (skirtao) is used of joyful leaping. John begins his mission of pointing to Christ before he is born; the Church sees him sanctified by the presence of the Lord (Catechism 717, 523).
“The mother of my Lord.”
In the Greek Old Testament “Lord” (Kyrios) translates the divine name. Elizabeth's words are a root of the title Mother of God (Theotokos), defined at the Council of Ephesus in 431 (Catechism 495).
The Magnificat.
Mary's song, named from its first word in Latin. It echoes the song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2:1–10) and many psalms, and is sung every day at Evening Prayer (Catechism 2619).
The date of the feast.

The Visitation was spread by the Franciscans in the thirteenth century and extended to the whole Church in 1389, on 2 July. The calendar reform of 1969 placed it on 31 May, between the Annunciation and the Birth of John the Baptist (St Paul VI, Marialis Cultus 7).
altar: Mary carried the hidden Christ to Elizabeth's house, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy. At this altar the same Lord comes hidden under the appearance of bread and wine, truly present, Body and Blood, soul and divinity. When we receive him, we too become bearers of Christ, sent out with haste to the homes of others.

Every Mass is a visitation: God comes to his people. With Elizabeth we may say before Communion, why has this happened to me, that my Lord comes to me? and with Mary, after Communion, my soul magnifies the Lord.
outline: Opening
Ask: when God gives you a great joy, what is the first thing you do with it?
Point 1 · Rejoice, daughter Zion
The Lord in your midst: Zephaniah's joy fulfilled in Mary.
Point 2 · With haste to the hill country
Mary carries Christ to serve; the new Ark of the Covenant.
Point 3 · Blessed is she who believed
Elizabeth, filled with the Spirit, greets the Mother of the Lord.
Point 4 · My soul magnifies the Lord
Mary's song of the lowly lifted up and the hungry filled.
Closing image
Two expectant mothers embracing in a doorway in the hills, and an unborn child leaping for joy.
Take-home line
“Blessed is she who believed.”
live: Visit someone
This week visit an elderly relative, a pregnant mother, or a neighbour who is alone, as Mary visited Elizabeth, and offer practical help.
Pray the Magnificat
Pray Luke 1:46–55 slowly each evening this week, as the Church does at Vespers.
Close the month of May
End the Marian month today by praying the Rosary as a family, the Joyful Mysteries if you can, and thanking Mary for her care.
Serve with haste
When you see a need today, do not delay: act on it at once, with joy.
fathers: St Ambrose (in substance)
Mary went with haste into the hill country, not because she doubted the angel, but because she rejoiced in the promise and was eager to serve. The grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts.
St Ambrose (in substance)

Let the soul of Mary be in each of us to magnify the Lord; let the spirit of Mary be in each of us to rejoice in God. If according to the flesh there is one mother of Christ, according to faith Christ is the fruit of all.
St Bede the Venerable (in substance)

It is a good and holy custom in the Church that this hymn of the Mother of God is sung every day at the evening office, so that the remembrance of the Lord's Incarnation may kindle the devotion of the faithful.
magis: Catechism 495
Mary, called in the Gospels “the mother of Jesus,” is acclaimed by Elizabeth as “the mother of my Lord”; she is truly Mother of God (Theotokos).
Catechism 148
The Virgin Mary most perfectly embodies the obedience of faith; Elizabeth greets her: “blessed is she who believed.”
Catechism 717
John the Baptist, filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb, rejoices at the coming of Christ.
Catechism 2619
The Magnificat is the song both of the Mother of God and of the Church.
Catechism 2676
The words of the Hail Mary come from the angel's greeting and Elizabeth's blessing; Mary is the Ark of the Covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells.
saints: The Visitation in the Church

The feast was first kept by the Franciscans, encouraged by St Bonaventure in 1263, and extended to the whole Latin Church by Pope Urban VI in 1389. It gives its name to the Order of the Visitation, founded in 1610 by St Francis de Sales and St Jane Frances de Chantal to unite prayer with gentle service.
St Elizabeth

Elizabeth, of the priestly family of Aaron, and her husband Zechariah were “righteous before God” (Luke 1:6). Filled with the Holy Spirit, she was the first to call Mary the mother of the Lord. Both are honoured as saints in the Roman Martyrology.
2027-05-31.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who, while the Blessed Virgin Mary was carrying your Son in her womb, inspired her to visit Elizabeth, grant us, we pray, that, faithful to the promptings of the Spirit, we may magnify your greatness with the Virgin Mary at all times. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you went with haste to serve, carrying Christ within you. Teach us your joy and your readiness. As this month of May ends, take our families under your care, and help us to bring Jesus to every home we enter. Amen.

quick: Peter entered the house of the Roman centurion Cornelius; God shows no partiality, and the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles, who were baptized.
God is love: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son.
Jesus: love one another as I have loved you; I have called you friends; I chose you to bear fruit that will last.
2027-05-02.action: Do one concrete act of love this week for someone outside your usual circle.
2027-05-02.question: Do I treat Jesus as a master to be obeyed from a distance, or as a friend who has told me everything?
catechism: Children, not slaves, responding to the love that came first.
kidsaint: St Athanasius

Athanasius was a bishop in Alexandria in Egypt, long ago. Some people said that Jesus was not really God. Athanasius said: Jesus is truly God, the Son of the Father! Because of this he was sent away from his home five times, but he never stopped telling the truth. Lesson: be brave and faithful to Jesus, even when others laugh or disagree.
2027-05-02.special: Sixth Sunday of Easter, Year B: Gloria and Creed; St Athanasius not kept; the readings of the Seventh Sunday may be used where the Ascension is on Sunday 9 May; Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Agapē

The Greek word the New Testament uses for the love that gives itself, the love God is (1 John 4:8) and the love Jesus commands (John 15:12). It is not first a feeling but a decision to seek the good of the other, even at a cost, learned from God's own love for us.

family.explain: Jesus tells us: I do not call you servants, I call you my friends! A friend tells you secrets and shares everything with you. Jesus shares with us everything his Father told him. And he asks us to love each other the way he loves us, even when it is hard. Peter learned that God's love is for people of every country and every language.
family.intention: We pray for families who are lonely or left out, and for people who have no friends.
family.ask: Ask: “What does a good friend do?” Then choose one way each of us can be a good friend to someone this week, especially someone who is alone.

illus: An illustration

At a hospital in Thiruvananthapuram, an elderly Muslim man lay alone after an accident; his family was working in the Gulf. In the next bed was a young Catholic from Kollam with a broken leg. For three weeks the young man read the newspaper aloud to him, shared the food his mother brought, and called the nurse at night when the old man could not sleep. On the day of discharge the old man held his hand and said: You are not my relative, but you behaved like my son. The young man said later that he had only remembered one line from the Sunday Mass: love one another as I have loved you.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us your friends. Keep us in your love, and teach us to love one another as you have loved us. Alleluia. Amen.
share: God shows no partiality (Acts 10:34). Are there people I quietly keep at a distance because of who they are?
Not that we loved God but that he loved us (1 John 4:10). When did I last feel deeply loved by God?
I have called you friends (John 15:15). What would change in my prayer if I spoke to Jesus as a friend?
pm.resp: The Lord has revealed to the nations his saving power.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome people of every nation, language and background, as Peter welcomed Cornelius.
For those who are excluded because of caste, race, religion or poverty, that they may find friends in Christ's disciples.
For all who are lonely, that they may know Jesus as their friend.
For those who lay down their lives for others: soldiers, nurses, firefighters, parents.
For our group, that our love for one another may be the fruit that lasts.
pm.close: Father, you are love, and you have made us friends of your Son. Pour out your Spirit on us and on all peoples, so that we may love one another as he has loved us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Corinth Paul lived and worked as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla, and preached in the synagogue every sabbath.
When some opposed him he went next door; Crispus, the synagogue official, believed with all his household.
Jesus: a little while, and you will not see me; you will have pain, but your pain will turn into joy.
2027-05-06.action: Offer your day's work to Christ before you begin it, and do one task with special care for his sake.
2027-05-06.question: Which pain in my life am I waiting for the Lord to turn into joy?
catechism: Hope that sustains us in trial.
kidsaint: St Dominic Savio

Dominic was a boy in Italy who went to Don Bosco's school. He was cheerful, loved games, and was a good friend to everyone. Once he stopped two boys who were going to fight with stones by holding up a small cross between them. He died when he was only fourteen. Lesson: you do not have to be grown up to be a saint; you can be holy and happy today.
2027-05-06.special: Easter weekday in India. Where the Ascension is kept today (the Vatican and many countries), it is a solemnity and holy day of obligation; in India it is celebrated on Sunday 9 May. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Transferred solemnity

A solemnity moved from its own day to another day, by the rules of the liturgical calendar or a decision of the bishops. The Ascension, the Epiphany and Corpus Christi are transferred to a Sunday in India so that all the faithful can take part.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends: soon you will be sad because you will not see me, but your sadness will turn into joy. It is like waiting for a baby to be born: there is pain first, then great happiness. When we are sad, Jesus is still with us, and he can turn our sad days into happy ones.
family.intention: We pray for everyone in our family and our street who is sad today, and for all who work hard with their hands to feed their families.
family.ask: Ask: “What job did each of us do today? Can we offer it to Jesus?” Then say together: Jesus, we give you our work.

illus: An illustration

In a coastal parish near Alappuzha a retired tailor kept a small shop near the church. He mended school uniforms at half price and never sent anyone away. When a young man who had stopped going to church came to have his trousers altered, the tailor talked with him while he measured and stitched, every week, about cricket, about his mother, and now and then about Jesus. He never preached. After a year the young man asked him to be his sponsor for Confirmation. At the parish feast he said: I did not come back because of a sermon. I came back because of a needle.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in the little while of our waiting, stay with us and turn our sorrow into joy. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them (Acts 18:3). How can my daily work become a place of witness?
Crispus became a believer in the Lord, together with all his household (Acts 18:8). Whose conversion am I praying for?
Your pain will turn into joy (John 16:20). Where have I seen God turn pain into joy, in my life or in someone else's?
pm.resp: The Lord has revealed to the nations his saving power.
interc: For all workers, especially daily-wage labourers, migrant workers and those without secure work, that their labour may be respected and justly paid.
For Christian couples who serve the Church together, like Aquila and Priscilla.
For good relations between Christians and Jews, and for an end to every form of antisemitism.
For all who are weeping and mourning today, that their pain may be turned into joy.
For our group, that we may wait for the Lord with patience and witness to him in our work.
pm.close: Father, your Son has gone ahead of us, and we wait in hope. Bless the work of our hands and turn our sorrows into the joy of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Forty days after the Resurrection, Jesus promised the Holy Spirit and sent the apostles to be his witnesses to the ends of the earth; then a cloud took him from their sight.
God seated Christ at his right hand, above every power, and made him head of the Church, his body.
The disciples went out and proclaimed the Gospel everywhere, while the Lord worked with them.
2027-05-09.action: Share one Gospel verse or message of hope with someone today, in person or on your phone, as an act of witness on World Communications Day.
2027-05-09.question: Am I standing and looking up, or am I going out as the Lord's witness?
catechism: Christ our High Priest intercedes for us.
kidsaint: St Carlo Acutis

Carlo was an Italian teenager who loved video games, football and computers. He also loved Jesus in the Eucharist and went to Mass every day. He used his computer skills to make a website about Eucharistic miracles that people still visit today. He died of leukaemia in 2006 at fifteen and was declared a saint in 2025. He said: the Eucharist is my highway to heaven. Lesson: you can use your phone and computer to share Jesus with the world.
2027-05-09.special: Solemnity of the Ascension (India). Gloria and Creed; Preface of the Ascension; World Communications Day; Seventh Sunday of Easter not celebrated this year in India. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Seated at the right hand of the Father

A phrase of the Creed from Psalm 110:1. It does not mean a place in the sky but that the risen Christ, in his glorified humanity, shares the glory, power and kingship of the Father, and intercedes for us there.

family.explain: Forty days after Easter Jesus took his friends to a hill, blessed them, and went up to heaven. A cloud hid him. Two angels said: why are you looking up at the sky? Jesus will come back! Now go and tell everyone about him. Jesus is with the Father, and he is also with us every day. Today is also Mother's Day in many places: we thank God for our mothers, and for Mary, the Mother of Jesus, who prayed with the apostles while they waited for the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries all over the world, for all who work in newspapers, television and the internet, and for our mothers.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we tell about Jesus this week?” Choose one person and pray for them together every night until Pentecost.

illus: An illustration

When a fisherman from Poovar took a job in the Gulf, his small daughter cried at the airport as the plane disappeared into the clouds. For a long time she would not eat. Her mother told her: Appa has not gone away from us; he has gone ahead for us. Every month money came home, and every evening a video call. Two years later the family moved into a small concrete house built with his wages. On the day it was blessed, the girl, now eight, said to the parish priest: Appa went away so he could prepare a place for us. The priest said: that is exactly what Jesus said on the day he went into the clouds.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, King of glory, lift up our hearts to you, and send us out as your witnesses. Come, Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Why do you stand looking up toward heaven? (Acts 1:11). Is my faith more gazing than going? Where is the Lord sending me?
He has made him the head over all things for the church, which is his body (Ephesians 1:22–23). How do I live as a member of Christ's Body in my parish?
The Lord worked with them and confirmed the message (Mark 16:20). When have I felt the Lord working with me?
pm.resp: God mounts his throne to shouts of joy: a blare of trumpets for the Lord.
interc: For the Church spread through the world, that she may witness to the risen and ascended Lord to the ends of the earth.
For all who work in the media and on the internet, that they may serve truth, peace and human dignity, and for Christians to use their phones and screens for good.
For missionaries, especially those working in difficult places, that the Lord may work with them.
For our mothers, living and dead, and for all mothers who are anxious for their children.
For our group, that we may pray with Mary in these days and receive the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.
pm.close: Almighty Father, your Son ascended to your right hand, our Head gone before us. Keep our hearts fixed on him, and send us his Spirit, so that we may be his witnesses everywhere. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Fifty days after Easter, on the feast of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came on the disciples with wind and fire, and they spoke so that every nation heard in its own language.
There are varieties of gifts but the same Spirit; no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Spirit, and in one Spirit we were baptised into one body.
On Easter evening the risen Jesus breathed on the apostles: Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive are forgiven.
2027-05-16.action: Pray the Sequence, Come, Holy Spirit, slowly today, and choose one gift you will use for others this week.
2027-05-16.question: Which room of my life is still behind locked doors, waiting for the Spirit's peace?
catechism: Pentecost: the Passover fulfilled, the Trinity revealed.
Confirmation perpetuates the grace of Pentecost.
The gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: Mary in the upper room

After Jesus went up to heaven, Mary, the Mother of Jesus, prayed with the apostles for nine days, waiting for the Holy Spirit. When the Spirit came like wind and fire, she was there with them. That is why we call her the Mother of the Church. Lesson: when we pray together, like a family with Mary, God gives us his Spirit.
2027-05-16.special: Pentecost Sunday, Year B: Gloria, Sequence (obligatory) and Creed; red vestments; double Alleluia at the dismissal; end of the Easter season; paschal candle moved to the baptistery; from tomorrow the Angelus.
term: Paraclete

From the Greek paraklētos, one called to stand beside you: advocate, helper, comforter. Jesus' name for the Holy Spirit in John 14 to 16. He is “another Advocate,” for Jesus himself is our Advocate with the Father (1 John 2:1).

family.explain: Fifty days after Easter, the friends of Jesus were praying together with Mary. Suddenly there was a noise like a strong wind, and little flames like fire came to rest on each of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit and were not afraid any more! They went out and spoke about Jesus, and people from many countries understood them in their own language. Today is the birthday of the Church. The same Holy Spirit came to us when we were baptised and confirmed.
family.intention: We pray for all who will be confirmed this year, for our parish, and for people who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What good gift has God given to each person in our family?” Let everyone say one gift they see in another. Then pray together: Come, Holy Spirit!

illus: An illustration

A parish in a Kerala town has Sunday Mass in Malayalam, but after a new factory opened nearby, many workers from Odisha, Jharkhand and Bihar began to come. They stood at the back and understood little. One Pentecost, the youth group asked a young worker to read the Gospel in Hindi after the Malayalam reading, and to lead a prayer of the faithful in his own language. An older parishioner said afterwards: for the first time I understood what Pentecost means. God did not make us all speak one language; he made us one family that listens in many.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. Send forth your Spirit, and renew the face of the earth. Amen.
share: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:4). When have I felt the Spirit give me courage I did not have by myself?
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good (1 Corinthians 12:7). What is my gift, and am I using it for others?
Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them (John 20:22–23). Is there forgiveness I need to receive, or to give?
pm.resp: Lord, send forth your Spirit, and renew the face of the earth.
interc: For the whole Church on her birthday, that the Holy Spirit may renew her in holiness, unity and missionary courage.
For the Pope, the bishops and all priests, that they may be faithful ministers of the Spirit's forgiveness.
For those preparing for Baptism and Confirmation, that they may open their hearts to the gifts of the Spirit.
For peoples divided by language, caste, race or religion, that the Spirit may help them understand and respect one another.
For the sick, the sad and the discouraged, that the Comforter may console them.
For our group, that each of us may discover and use our gifts for the common good.
pm.close: Father, on this day you sent the Holy Spirit upon the apostles gathered with Mary. Pour out the same Spirit upon us, and make us witnesses of your Son to the ends of the earth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses: has anything so great ever happened? The Lord is God in heaven and on earth; there is no other.
Paul: the Spirit makes us children of God; in us he cries “Abba! Father!”; we are heirs with Christ.
The risen Jesus sends the eleven to baptise all nations in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and promises to be with us always.
2027-05-23.action: Make the sign of the cross slowly and with attention every time you pray this week.
2027-05-23.question: Do I live as a child of the Father, a brother or sister of the Son, and a temple of the Holy Spirit?
catechism: The Trinity, the central mystery of faith.
One God in three distinct Persons.
Called to be a dwelling of the Trinity.
kidsaint: St Patrick and the shamrock

St Patrick brought the Gospel to Ireland about sixteen hundred years ago. A well-loved story, told many centuries after him, says that he picked up a shamrock, a little plant with three leaves on one stem, to explain the Holy Trinity: three leaves, yet one plant. No picture can fully show who God is, but the story helped people remember that God is one, and that there are three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Lesson: we can learn about God even from small things in nature.
2027-05-23.special: Solemnity of the Most Holy Trinity, Year B: Gloria and Creed; it takes the place of the Eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time; Angelus at noon.
term: Consubstantial

From the Latin consubstantialis, translating the Greek homoousios, the word chosen by the Council of Nicaea (325): the Son is of the same substance, the same being, as the Father. It says that the Son is truly God, not a lesser being, and is professed in the Creed at every Sunday Mass.

family.explain: God is one, but God is not lonely. God is the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, loving one another for ever. When we were baptised, we were welcomed into that family of love. That is why we make the sign of the cross: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Our family, where we love and forgive each other, is meant to be a small picture of God's family.
family.intention: We pray for all children who will be baptised this year, for their parents and godparents, and for missionaries who bring the Gospel to all nations.
family.ask: Ask: “When is our family most like God's family of love?” Then make the sign of the cross together, slowly, and say what each name means to you.

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish near Mangaluru asked her class of ten-year-olds how God can be one and three. After many guesses, a quiet girl said: in our house there is my father, my mother and me. We are three. But when we sit together for prayer at night, we are one family, and it is the love that makes us one. The teacher told her that no picture of the Trinity is perfect, because God is not a family of three gods. But she added: you have understood the most important thing. God is love, and love is never alone.

pm.open: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
share: Has anything so great as this ever happened? (Deuteronomy 4:32). What great things has God done in my life that I should remember today?
When we cry, “Abba! Father!” it is that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God (Romans 8:15–16). Do I pray as a child, or as a stranger?
I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matthew 28:20). Where do I need to remember this promise this week?
pm.resp: Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a sign of the communion of the Holy Trinity in the world.
For all who will be baptised this year, and for their parents and godparents.
For missionaries, catechists and all who make disciples of all nations.
For families, that they may grow as communities of love, an image of the Trinity.
For those who doubt, that the risen Lord may come near to them as he came to the eleven.
For our group, that the Spirit may teach us to pray “Abba, Father” with trust.
pm.close: Most Holy Trinity, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, one God, we adore you and give you thanks; keep us always in your love. Amen.

quick: At Sinai Moses sealed the covenant by dashing blood on the altar and on the people: See the blood of the covenant.
Christ, our high priest, entered heaven with his own blood, and his blood purifies our conscience to worship the living God.
At the Last Supper Jesus took bread and the cup and said: This is my body; this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
2027-05-30.action: Spend ten minutes this week in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament.
2027-05-30.question: Do I receive Holy Communion as if I truly believed that it is Jesus himself?
catechism: The real presence of Christ in the Eucharist.
Why do we adore the Blessed Sacrament?
kidsaint: St Carlo Acutis

Carlo was a boy in Italy who loved computers, video games and his dog. But most of all he loved Jesus in the Eucharist. He went to Mass every day he could, and he called the Eucharist his highway to heaven. He used his computer skills to make a website about Eucharistic miracles from all over the world, so that more people would believe that Jesus is really there. He died of leukaemia when he was only fifteen, in 2006, and Pope Leo XIV declared him a saint in 2025. Lesson: you can love Jesus in the Eucharist with all your heart, even while you are young and enjoy ordinary things.
2027-05-30.special: Solemnity of the Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ (Year B), kept on this Sunday in India in place of the Ninth Sunday in Ordinary Time. Gloria and Creed. Sequence Lauda Sion (optional). Eucharistic procession and Benediction where possible.
term: Transubstantiation

The word the Church uses for the change that takes place at the consecration of the Mass: the whole substance of the bread becomes the Body of Christ and the whole substance of the wine becomes his Blood, while the appearances (colour, taste, shape) of bread and wine remain (Council of Trent; Catechism 1376). Jesus is therefore present not as a symbol but truly, really and substantially.

family.explain: At the Last Supper Jesus took bread and said: this is my body. He took the cup and said: this is my blood. Jesus gave himself to his friends, and he still gives himself to us at every Mass. The Host looks like bread, but it is really Jesus. That is why we kneel, we are quiet, and we say Amen when we receive him.
family.intention: We pray for children preparing for their First Holy Communion, and for all who cannot go to Mass because they are sick or far away.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family show Jesus that we believe he is really present in the Holy Eucharist?” Then plan a short family visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week.

illus: An illustration

In a coastal parish near Kollam the Corpus Christi procession used to pass the house of an old fisherman who had not been to church for thirty years. Every year his neighbours put out lamps and flowers; he sat on his veranda with his back turned. One year, when the monstrance stopped for Benediction right in front of his gate, his little granddaughter ran out and knelt in the road. He went out to bring her back, and found himself kneeling beside her. The next week he went to confession. He said afterwards: I had stopped going to him, so he came to me. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, truly present in the Most Holy Sacrament, we adore you. Gather us around your table and make us one body in you. Amen.
share: See the blood of the covenant (Exodus 24:8). What does it mean to me that God has made me part of his family by the blood of Christ?
How much more will the blood of Christ purify our conscience (Hebrews 9:14). Do I bring to the Eucharist a heart that wants to be purified?
Take; this is my body (Mark 14:22). How do I prepare for Holy Communion, and how do I give thanks afterwards?
pm.resp: I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may always draw her life from the Eucharist and adore the Lord with deep faith.
For priests, who stand at the altar in the person of Christ, that they may celebrate the holy mysteries with reverence and love.
For children preparing for First Holy Communion, and for their parents and catechists.
For the sick, the elderly and prisoners who cannot come to Mass, that they may receive the Lord through those who bring Communion.
For the hungry of our country, that those who receive the Bread of Life may share their bread.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave us his Body and Blood as the food of eternal life. May we who receive him become what we receive. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul took the young Timothy as companion; the Holy Spirit closed the way to Asia and Bithynia.
In a night vision a Macedonian pleaded, “Come over and help us,” and the Gospel crossed into Europe.
Jesus warned that the world which hated him would hate his disciples; today is also St Joseph the Worker and the first day of Mary's month.
2027-05-01.action: Thank one worker today by name, and offer your own work to God at the start of the day.
2027-05-01.question: When God closes a door for me, do I complain, or do I look for where the Spirit is leading?
kidsaint: St Joseph the Worker

Joseph was a carpenter in the village of Nazareth. Every day he worked with wood, making doors, tables and ploughs, and Jesus learned to work beside him. Joseph did not become famous, but he worked hard and honestly to look after Jesus and Mary. Lesson: when we do our work well, even homework and helping at home, we can offer it to God like St Joseph.

family.explain: Paul wanted to go to some places, but the Holy Spirit said no. Then one night Paul had a dream of a man saying, “Come and help us!” So Paul and his friends went across the sea to a new country and told people about Jesus. Today we also remember St Joseph, who worked as a carpenter, and we begin May, Mother Mary's month.
family.intention: We pray for fathers and mothers who work hard for the family, and for people who have no job.
family.ask: Ask: “What work can each of us offer to God this week, like St Joseph?” Begin a family Rosary or one decade every evening this May.

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Thrissur had everything arranged for a job abroad. Twice the visa was refused, and he was bitter. In the waiting months he began teaching mathematics in the evenings to children of daily-wage workers in his parish, just to fill the time. Twenty children came, then fifty. When at last the visa came through, he turned it down. He says now: I thought God had shut the door; he had only shown me the right one.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, lead us as you led Paul. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
share: The Spirit of Jesus did not allow them (Acts 16:7). When has a closed door in my life turned out to be God's guidance?
Come over to Macedonia and help us (Acts 16:9). Whose cry for help am I being asked to hear?
If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you (John 15:18). Have I ever been mocked or left out because of my faith? How did I respond?
pm.resp: Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth.
interc: For missionaries who go where they are needed, that they may follow the Holy Spirit with courage.
For workers, especially daily-wage labourers, migrants and those in unsafe jobs, that they may receive a just wage and be treated with dignity.
For the unemployed and for young people looking for their first job.
For Christians who suffer hostility because of their faith.
For our families, that this month of May may be a month of prayer with the Blessed Virgin Mary.
pm.close: Father, you call us to share in your work of creation and to follow your Son, the carpenter's son. Through the prayers of St Joseph, make our work holy and our hearts open to your Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul hands on the oldest creed: Christ died, was buried, rose on the third day, and appeared to Cephas, the Twelve, more than five hundred, James and all the apostles.
Their voice goes out through all the earth: the apostles' witness reaches the ends of the world.
Philip asks, “Show us the Father”; Jesus answers, “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
2027-05-03.action: Invite one person this week to “come and see,” as Philip did.
2027-05-03.question: Am I still looking past Jesus for God, when the Father is showing himself to me in Jesus?
catechism: Christ's whole life reveals the Father.
kidsaint: St Philip and St James

Philip was one of the first friends of Jesus. When he met Jesus, he ran to his friend Nathanael and said: come and see! James was another of the twelve apostles; he led the Christians in Jerusalem and taught that if we love Jesus we must help people who need it. Lesson: bring your friends to Jesus like Philip, and show your faith by kind actions like James.
2027-05-03.special: Feast of Sts Philip and James, Apostles: Gloria, proper readings, red vestments; the Easter weekday is replaced.
term: Apostle

From the Greek apostolos, “one who is sent.” The Twelve were chosen by Jesus to be with him and to be sent out to preach (Mark 3:14). They are the witnesses of his Resurrection, the foundation of the Church, and their mission continues through the bishops, their successors.

family.explain: Philip asked Jesus: Show us God the Father! Jesus said: Philip, you have been with me so long! When you see me, you see the Father. Jesus shows us what God is like: kind, forgiving, loving the poor and the children. Today we remember two apostles, Philip and James, who told the whole world about Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for bishops, the successors of the apostles, and especially for our own bishop.
family.ask: Ask: “What does Jesus show us about God?” Each one says one thing, for example: God forgives, God loves children, God heals.

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Kottayam was asked by a Hindu colleague, a close friend for many years: What is your God really like? She did not know how to begin. The next week she gave her friend a small copy of the Gospel of Luke and said: Read about Jesus. That is what God is like. Some months later the friend returned it, much underlined, and said: I always thought God was far away; this one comes to eat with sinners. They still talk about it over tea. The teacher says she learned that day from St Philip: you do not have to win an argument; you only have to say, come and see.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied. Through the prayers of St Philip and St James, make us witnesses of your Resurrection. Amen.
share: Then he appeared to James (1 Corinthians 15:7). Who handed on the faith to me, and have I thanked God for them?
Lord, show us the Father (John 14:8). What is my deepest question about God?
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father (John 14:9). Which Gospel scene shows me most clearly what God is like?
pm.resp: Their voice goes out through all the earth.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops, successors of the apostles, that they may hand on the faith faithfully.
For missionaries who carry the apostles' voice to the ends of the earth.
For all who are searching for God, that they may find the Father in the face of Jesus.
For Christians in Turkey and the Middle East, in the lands where Philip and James preached.
For our group, that like Philip we may bring others to Jesus, and like James we may live what we believe.
pm.close: Father, through the apostles you handed on to us the good news of your Son's Resurrection. Keep us faithful to their teaching, and let us see your face in Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Philippi Paul and Silas were beaten and jailed; at midnight they prayed and sang, and an earthquake opened the doors.
Paul stopped the jailer from killing himself; the jailer asked how to be saved and was baptized with his household.
Jesus says it is better for the disciples that he goes away, so that the Advocate may come.
2027-05-04.action: Turn one moment of frustration today into a moment of praise.
2027-05-04.question: Do I believe that the Lord's “going away” in my life can make room for a greater gift?

family.explain: Paul and Silas were put in prison for talking about Jesus. Their feet were locked. But at midnight, instead of crying, they sang songs to God! Then an earthquake opened all the doors. The jailer was so amazed that he asked to know Jesus, and his whole family was baptized that night.
family.intention: We pray for people who are in prison, and for their families waiting at home.
family.ask: Ask: “What song can we sing to God when we are sad?” Choose one hymn and sing it together tonight.

illus: An illustration

Blessed Rani Maria, the Franciscan Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy near Perumbavoor, worked among the poor in Madhya Pradesh and was murdered in 1995. Her killer, Samundar Singh, was sent to prison. There, years later, her own sister, Sister Selmy Paul, visited him, called him brother, and tied a rakhi on his wrist. He wept, asked forgiveness, and was later received with love by the family of the one he had killed. Like the jailer of Philippi, a man in the darkness found his way to salvation because Christians answered violence with mercy.

pm.open: Lord, at midnight Paul and Silas sang your praises. Teach us to praise you in every hour, and send us your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God (Acts 16:25). What do I do in my midnight hours?
Sirs, what must I do to be saved? (Acts 16:30). Who around me is asking this question, perhaps without words?
It is to your advantage that I go away (John 16:7). What loss in my life has made room for a greater gift?
pm.resp: Your right hand delivers me, O Lord.
interc: For prisoners and prison chaplains, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For those who are thinking of harming themselves, that someone may say to them, as Paul did: do not harm yourself.
For families who are preparing for Baptism, that the joy of the jailer's household may be theirs.
For victims of violence and for those who have hurt them, that mercy may open the way to conversion.
For our group, that the Holy Spirit may fill us as we prepare for the Ascension and Pentecost.
pm.close: Father, you answered Paul and Silas at midnight. Stretch out your hand over all who suffer, and send us the Advocate, as your Son promised. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the Areopagus in Athens Paul began from the altar “To an unknown god” and proclaimed the Creator, in whom we live and move and have our being.
When he spoke of the resurrection, some scoffed, but Dionysius, Damaris and others believed.
Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all the truth.
2027-05-05.action: Pray today for one friend of another faith by name, and treat them with the respect Paul showed the Athenians.
2027-05-05.question: Do I speak of my faith with both respect for others and courage about the Resurrection?

family.explain: Paul visited Athens, a city full of temples and statues. He saw an altar that said: To an unknown god. Paul said: I will tell you about this God! He made the world, he gives us life and breath, and he is very close to each of us. Then Paul told them about Jesus, who rose from the dead. Some laughed, but some believed.
family.intention: We pray for our neighbours and friends of other religions, that we may live together in peace and respect.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show our friends of other faiths that Jesus loves them?”

illus: An illustration

Robert de Nobili, an Italian Jesuit who came to Madurai in 1606, saw that people kept their distance from the Gospel because it seemed foreign. He learned Tamil and Sanskrit, studied the Indian scriptures, dressed and lived simply as a sannyasi, and spoke of Christ in words his hearers could understand. Some of his methods were debated in his own day and were examined in Rome, which in 1623 allowed them with conditions. Like Paul at the Areopagus, he looked for the doors already present in a culture's search for God, and walked through them with the name of Jesus.

pm.open: Spirit of truth, guide us into all the truth, and teach us to speak of Jesus with respect and courage. Amen.
share: I see how extremely religious you are in every way (Acts 17:22). How do I look at people of other faiths?
He is not far from each one of us (Acts 17:27). When did I last feel how close God is?
He will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). What truth of faith do I want the Holy Spirit to make clearer to me?
pm.resp: Heaven and earth are full of your glory.
interc: For dialogue between Christians and people of other religions in India, that it may grow in truth and friendship.
For teachers, scholars and students in universities, that they may search for God and find him.
For those who scoff at the Resurrection, that one day they may say, we will hear you again about this.
For catechists and preachers, that the Spirit of truth may guide their words.
For our group, that we may be ready to give an account of the hope that is in us.
pm.close: Father, in you we live and move and have our being. Send the Spirit of truth to guide your Church, and make us witnesses of the risen Christ to every people. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In a night vision the Lord told Paul: do not be afraid, speak, for I am with you; Paul stayed eighteen months in Corinth.
Gallio refused to judge a dispute about the Jewish law, and Paul was able to continue his work.
Jesus: like a woman in labour you have pain now, but I will see you again, and no one will take your joy from you.
2027-05-07.action: Pray an act of consecration to the Sacred Heart with your family tonight, and begin the novena to the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-07.question: Where am I silent out of fear when the Lord is asking me to speak?
catechism: Called to witness by word and deed.
kidsaint: St Margaret Mary Alacoque

Margaret Mary was a French sister who loved to pray before Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Jesus showed her his Heart, burning with love for all people, and asked people to receive him in Holy Communion on the first Friday of the month. Lesson: Jesus' Heart is full of love for you; you can give him your heart too.
2027-05-07.special: Easter weekday; First Friday (Sacred Heart devotion). The novena to the Holy Spirit may begin today. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: First Friday

The custom of going to confession and receiving Holy Communion on the first Friday of the month, in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and in reparation for sins. It goes back to the revelations to St Margaret Mary in the seventeenth century.

family.explain: Jesus said that his friends would be sad for a while, like a mother when her baby is being born. But when the baby comes, the mother is so happy that she forgets the pain. Jesus' cross was painful, but from it came new life for us. Today is First Friday: we remember how much Jesus' Heart loves us.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting a baby, for babies being born today, and for all who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family needs courage today?” Place your hands on that person's shoulder and pray: Jesus, be with them; do not be afraid.

illus: An illustration

A senior nurse who worked for thirty years in the labour room of a mission hospital in Thrissur used to say the same thing to every frightened young mother: in one hour you will forget all this, I promise you. The mothers never believed her during the pain, and always laughed about it afterwards with the baby in their arms. On the first Friday of every month she went to the hospital chapel before her shift. When a young doctor asked her why, she said: there I look at a Heart that went through labour for all of us. It helps me to tell the mothers the truth.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Heart was pierced for us. Take away our fear and give us the joy that no one can take from us. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent (Acts 18:9). What am I afraid to say for Jesus?
There are many in this city who are my people (Acts 18:10). How do I look at my town or city: as hopeless, or as a place where God has his people?
No one will take your joy from you (John 16:22). What kind of joy do I live on: the kind that goes, or the kind that stays?
pm.resp: God is king of all the earth.
interc: For Christians who are afraid to speak of their faith, that the Lord may stand by them.
For judges and magistrates, that they may protect religious freedom and the rights of all.
For expectant mothers and for children about to be born.
For all who are devoted to the Sacred Heart, that they may grow in love and reparation.
For our group, beginning the novena to the Holy Spirit with Mary.
pm.close: Father, from the pierced Heart of your Son you gave birth to your Church. Fill us with the joy of the Resurrection, which no one can take from us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul set out again through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
In Ephesus, Priscilla and Aquila took the eloquent Apollos aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately.
Jesus: ask the Father in my name and you will receive; the Father himself loves you.
2027-05-08.action: Encourage one person whose faith is tired, by a visit, a call or a short message.
2027-05-08.question: Do I pray to the Father as someone who knows that he loves me?
catechism: Asking in the name of Jesus.
Mary at prayer with the infant Church.
kidsaint: Sts Aquila and Priscilla

Aquila and Priscilla were a husband and wife who made tents. They let St Paul live with them, worked with him, and opened their home for Christians to pray. When a clever preacher called Apollos did not know everything about Jesus, they invited him home and taught him kindly. Lesson: families can be missionaries too, and we can help others gently, without making them feel small.
2027-05-08.special: Easter weekday; Saturday in honour of Our Lady. In India, this evening's Mass is the Vigil Mass of the Ascension. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: In my name
To ask “in the name of Jesus” is to pray as his disciple, united with him, trusting in his authority and seeking his will. The liturgy ends its prayers “through Christ our Lord” for this reason.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends: ask the Father in my name, and he will give it to you. And then he said something beautiful: the Father himself loves you. God is not a stranger we must convince. He is a Father who already loves us, more than any parent loves a child.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to believe that God loves them, and for Christian families who open their homes to others.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we want to ask our Father for today?” Pray together, each beginning: Father, in the name of Jesus...

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kollam a young seminarian on his summer break was asked to preach at a weekday Mass. He spoke with great fire but said something about confession that was not quite right. After Mass an elderly couple, both retired teachers, invited him home for tea. Over banana fritters they gently opened the Catechism with him and showed him what the Church teaches. He was embarrassed for a moment, then grateful. Years later, as a parish priest, he told the story at their golden jubilee: they did not shame me from the pew; they corrected me at their table. That is how I learned to correct others.

pm.open: Father, in the name of Jesus we come to you, knowing that you love us. Send us your Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
share: He went from place to place, strengthening all the disciples (Acts 18:23). Whom can I strengthen this week?
They took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately (Acts 18:26). How do I correct others, and how do I accept correction?
The Father himself loves you (John 16:27). Do I really believe this, and how does it change my prayer?
pm.resp: God is king of all the earth.
interc: For missionaries and catechists who strengthen young churches.
For Christian couples who serve the Church together, and for all who open their homes to prayer and hospitality.
For preachers and teachers of the faith, that they may be both zealous and humble.
For those who find it hard to believe that God loves them.
For our group, waiting for the Holy Spirit with Mary, the Mother of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son goes to you and you love us in him. Hear the prayers we make in his name and fill us with his joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Ephesus Paul found disciples who had not even heard of the Holy Spirit; he baptized them in the name of Jesus and laid his hands on them, and the Spirit came upon them.
Paul spoke boldly in the synagogue for three months about the kingdom of God.
Jesus warned that the disciples would scatter, but said: take courage; I have conquered the world.
2027-05-10.action: Find out the date of your Confirmation and thank God for it today with the prayer “Come, Holy Spirit.”
2027-05-10.question: Do I live as someone who has received the Holy Spirit, or as one who has hardly heard of him?
catechism: The laying on of hands in Acts.
kidsaint: St Damien of Molokai

Father Damien was a priest from Belgium who went to an island in Hawaii where people with leprosy had been sent away from their families. Nobody wanted to go there. He built houses, a church and a school, dressed their wounds and played with the children. In the end he caught leprosy too, and he said: now I am one of you. Lesson: the Holy Spirit gives us courage to love people that others are afraid of.
2027-05-10.special: Easter weekday; St John of Avila (optional memorial). Novena to the Holy Spirit. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Confirmation

The sacrament that completes baptismal grace by the special outpouring of the Holy Spirit, given by the anointing with chrism on the forehead with the laying on of the hand and the words “Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.” In the Latin Church it is usually conferred by the bishop.

family.explain: Paul met some believers in Ephesus and asked them: did you receive the Holy Spirit? They said: we have never even heard of the Holy Spirit! So Paul baptized them in Jesus' name, put his hands on their heads and prayed, and the Holy Spirit came on them. We received the Holy Spirit in Baptism and Confirmation. He lives in us and helps us to be brave and good.
family.intention: We pray for children and young people preparing for Confirmation, and for all who are being persecuted for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we need courage in our family?” Pray together for one another: Holy Spirit, make us brave.

illus: An illustration

A Confirmation class in a parish in Ernakulam was asked by the catechist to write one sentence about the Holy Spirit. Most wrote what they had learned: the third Person of the Holy Trinity. One boy wrote: I do not know who he is. The catechist did not scold him. She asked the whole class to pray for one minute every evening, Come, Holy Spirit, and to note anything that happened. Three weeks later the same boy wrote: I apologized to my brother, and I did not want to. I think that was him.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers? (Acts 19:2). How would I answer Paul's question today?
When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them (Acts 19:6). What do I remember of my Confirmation, and how has it borne fruit?
Take courage; I have conquered the world! (John 16:33). Where do I need the courage of Christ this week?
pm.resp: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.
interc: For all who will receive Confirmation this year, that they may be filled with the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
For Christians who are persecuted or discriminated against because of their faith, that they may take courage in Christ.
For priests, that through the prayers of St John of Avila they may be holy, learned and full of love for the Eucharist.
For orphans, widows and the lonely, that the Church may be a home for them.
For our group, that in these days before Pentecost we may come to know the Holy Spirit more deeply.
pm.close: Father, your Son has conquered the world. Pour out on us the Spirit of courage and peace, so that we may witness to him without fear. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Miletus Paul said farewell to the elders of Ephesus: he had served with humility and tears and held nothing back.
He was going to Jerusalem, bound by the Spirit, willing to lose his life if only he could finish his course.
Jesus prayed: Father, the hour has come; this is eternal life, to know you and the one you have sent.
2027-05-11.action: Finish today one task or duty you have been tempted to leave half done, and offer it to the Lord.
2027-05-11.question: Do I see eternal life as something far away, or as knowing and loving God now?
kidsaint: St Ignatius of Laconi

Ignatius was a Capuchin brother on the island of Sardinia in Italy. Every day for forty years he walked the streets with a bag, asking for food for the friars and for the poor. He was always gentle and smiling, and he helped sick people and children he met on the way. Lesson: even a simple job, done with love every day, can make you a saint.
2027-05-11.special: Easter weekday; the Gospels from today until Thursday come from the priestly prayer of Jesus (John 17). Novena to the Holy Spirit. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: Presbyter
From the Greek presbyteros, “elder”: in the New Testament a leader of a local church (Acts 20:17). Our word “priest” comes from it. Priests share in the ministry of the bishop as his co-workers.

family.explain: Before he died, Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed to his Father for his friends. He said that eternal life means knowing God, not just knowing about him, but loving him and being his friend. Jesus prays for us too, every day, from heaven.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all priests, and for missionaries who have left their homes for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get to know Jesus better as a family?” Choose one way, such as reading a short Gospel passage after dinner, and try it this week.

illus: An illustration

When an old priest in a hill parish in Idukki was transferred after eighteen years, the church was full for his farewell Mass. He did not speak about the buildings he had put up. He said: I tried to tell you the whole truth, even when you did not like it, and I tried to visit every house. If I failed anyone, forgive me. Then he asked the people to pray for the new priest. Afterwards an old woman who had often argued with him said: he scolded us, but he wept for us too. We always knew he loved us.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you pray for us to the Father. Let us know you and the Father, and so have eternal life. Come, Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Serving the Lord with all humility and with tears (Acts 20:19). Whom do I serve with real love, even when it costs me?
If only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24). What is the course the Lord has given me, and am I running it?
This is eternal life, that they may know you (John 17:3). How well do I know God, not only about him?
pm.resp: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.
interc: For bishops and priests, that they may shepherd the Church with humility, courage and love, holding nothing back.
For missionaries who have left home for the Gospel, and for those who suffer imprisonment for their faith.
For those facing the last part of their life's course, that they may finish it with faith and peace.
For all who seek God, that they may come to know him and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.
For our group, that we may be kept in the name of the Father and receive the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we may know you and be kept in your name. Grant that we may finish our course with joy and come to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Miletus Paul said farewell to the elders of Ephesus: keep watch over the flock that Christ bought with his blood.
He reminded them of the Lord's saying: it is more blessed to give than to receive; they wept and prayed together on the shore.
Jesus prayed for his disciples: protect them from the evil one, sanctify them in the truth, as you sent me, so I send them.
2027-05-12.action: Give something today, quietly, without waiting for thanks.
2027-05-12.question: Do I belong to the world, or do I live in the world as one who belongs to God?
kidsaint: St Pancras

Pancras was a boy of about fourteen who lived in Rome long ago. When Christians were being arrested, he did not hide his faith in Jesus. He was put to death for being a Christian, and he is a patron of children and young people. Lesson: you are never too young to be brave for Jesus.

family.explain: St Paul had to say goodbye to his friends in Ephesus, and they cried and hugged him. Before he left he reminded them of something Jesus said: it is more blessed to give than to receive. Giving makes us happier than getting! Jesus also prayed for his friends that God would protect them and make them holy.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and our bishop, and for all who have to say goodbye to people they love.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us give to someone else today?”

illus: An illustration

A parish priest in a fishing village near Kollam was transferred after nine years. On his last Sunday he did not speak about himself. He handed each family a small card with the words of Acts 20:32 and said: I commend you to God and to the message of his grace. He reminded them that the parish had belonged to Christ before he came, and would belong to Christ after he left. Years later, many homes still kept that card near the family altar.

pm.open: Holy Father, keep us in your name, sanctify us in the truth, and send us into the world. Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock (Acts 20:28). For whom has God made me responsible, and how am I watching over them?
It is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). When did I last experience the joy of giving?
I am not asking you to take them out of the world (John 17:15). Where do I find it hard to be a Christian in the world around me?
pm.resp: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.
interc: For our Pope, our bishops and our priests, that the Holy Spirit may make them watchful shepherds of the flock.
For Christians tempted to give up their faith under pressure, that they may have the courage of Nereus, Achilleus and Pancras.
For those who are saying goodbye to family, friends or their homeland, that God may comfort them.
For all who work with their hands to support their families.
For our group, that we may be one as the Father and the Son are one, and wait together for the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we might be one and holy in the truth. Hear his prayer in us, and send us the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Before the council, Paul declared that he was on trial for the hope of the resurrection; the assembly was divided.
In the night the risen Lord stood near him: Keep up your courage; you must bear witness also in Rome.
Jesus prayed that all who believe through the apostles may be one, so that the world may believe; Our Lady of Fatima asked for prayer, conversion and peace.
2027-05-13.action: Pray one decade of the Rosary today for peace and for the unity of all Christians.
2027-05-13.question: Am I a builder of unity, or of division, in my family and parish?
kidsaint: Our Lady of Fatima

In 1917 three children in Portugal, Lucia, Francisco and Jacinta, were looking after sheep when they saw a beautiful Lady shining with light. She was the Mother of Jesus. She asked them to pray the Rosary every day for peace in the world and to love Jesus very much. Francisco and Jacinta are now saints! Lesson: children's prayers are powerful, and Mary loves to hear them.

family.explain: Before he died, Jesus prayed for his friends, and for us too! He asked his Father that we may all be one, loving each other like a family, so that everyone may believe in him. Paul was in danger, but Jesus came to him in the night and said: be brave! At Fatima, Mary asked three children to pray the Rosary for peace.
family.intention: We pray for peace in the world, for families that are divided, and for the unity of all Christians.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to make peace with today?” Pray a decade of the Rosary together.

illus: An illustration

On the first anniversary of the attack on his life, St John Paul II went to Fatima to thank Our Lady. Later the bullet that had been removed from his body was placed in the crown of the statue of Our Lady of Fatima, where it still is. A Pope who had been shot did not speak of revenge; he forgave the man who tried to kill him, visited him in prison, and gave the glory to God and to Mary's care.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you prayed that we may all be one. Stand near us, give us courage, and make us one in you. Mary, Queen of Peace, pray for us. Amen.
share: Keep up your courage! (Acts 23:11). When have I felt the Lord standing near me in a dark time?
I keep the Lord always before me (Psalm 16:8). What helps me keep the Lord before me during the day?
That they may all be one (John 17:21). Where do I see division among Christians, and what can I do to heal it?
pm.resp: Protect me, O God, for in you I take refuge.
interc: For all Christians, that the prayer of Jesus may be fulfilled and we may become completely one.
For Christians on trial or in prison for their faith, that the Lord may stand near them.
For peace in the world, especially in lands at war, through the prayers of Our Lady of Fatima.
For sinners and for those far from God, as Mary asked the children of Fatima.
For our group, that the Holy Spirit may find us praying together with Mary when Pentecost comes.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed for us on the night before he died. Make us one in your love, so that the world may believe that you sent him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: After the Ascension the apostles, praying with Mary, chose Matthias by lot to take the place of Judas among the Twelve.
The one chosen had to have been with Jesus from his baptism to the Ascension and be a witness of the resurrection.
Jesus says: you did not choose me but I chose you; I call you friends; love one another as I have loved you.
2027-05-14.action: Tell one person today, in a sentence, why you believe that Jesus is risen.
2027-05-14.question: Do I see my faith as my own choice, or as the Lord's choice of me in friendship?
catechism: The Twelve, representing the tribes of Israel.
The apostolic Church built on the apostles.
Love one another as I have loved you.
kidsaint: St Matthias

Matthias followed Jesus for a long time, from the River Jordan to the day Jesus went up to heaven, but nobody wrote his name down. After Judas left, the apostles needed a twelfth apostle. They prayed, and God chose Matthias! Lesson: even if nobody notices you, Jesus sees you, and he has a special job just for you.
2027-05-14.special: St Matthias, Apostle. Feast: Gloria; red vestments; the weekday readings give way.
term: Apostle

From the Greek apostolos, one who is sent. In the strict sense, the Twelve chosen by Jesus (with Matthias in the place of Judas), and Paul. The Church is called apostolic because she is built on their witness, keeps their teaching, and is led by their successors, the bishops.

family.explain: After Jesus went back to heaven, there were only eleven apostles, because Judas had left. Jesus had chosen twelve, so they needed one more. They chose two good men who had been with Jesus all the time, prayed to God, and asked him to show which one he wanted. God chose Matthias. Jesus says to us too: you did not choose me, I chose you, and I call you my friends.
family.intention: We pray for our bishop, who takes the place of the apostles today, and for young people whom Jesus is calling to be priests and sisters.
family.ask: Ask: “Jesus calls us his friends. What do good friends do for each other?”

illus: An illustration

In cricket there is a player called the twelfth man. He comes to every match, carries the drinks, and waits on the edge of the field, often without being noticed. When a player is injured, he is the one who runs in to take the empty place. Matthias was a little like that: for years he followed Jesus at the edge of the story, never named. When the place among the Twelve was empty, he was ready, because he had been there all along. But unlike a twelfth man, he did not step in for a while; the Lord chose him for life.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you chose Matthias to be a witness of your resurrection. You have chosen us too and called us friends. Fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: One of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection (Acts 1:22). How am I a witness to the risen Jesus in my daily life?
Lord, you know everyone's heart (Acts 1:24). Do I pray before I make important decisions?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change me to know that the Lord chose me?
pm.resp: He raises the poor from the dust, to make them sit with princes.
interc: For our Pope and all the bishops, successors of the apostles, that they may be faithful witnesses of the resurrection.
For those who serve the Church without being noticed, that the Lord may reward their faithfulness.
For young people discerning a vocation, that they may hear the Lord's choice and answer generously.
For all who must make difficult decisions, that they may seek God's will in prayer.
For our group, that we may love one another as Jesus loved us, and wait together for the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you completed the college of the apostles by choosing Saint Matthias. Keep your Church faithful to their witness, and number us among your friends. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Acts ends in Rome: Paul, a prisoner, welcomes all who come and proclaims the kingdom with boldness and without hindrance.
He tells the Jewish leaders of Rome that he is bound for the sake of the hope of Israel.
John's Gospel ends: Jesus tells Peter not to worry about the beloved disciple but to follow him; the Gospel rests on that disciple's true witness.
2027-05-15.action: Each time you compare yourself with someone today, turn it into a prayer: Lord, I will follow you.
2027-05-15.question: Am I so busy watching other people's roads that I forget to follow Jesus on mine?

family.explain: After Jesus rose, Peter asked him about John: Lord, what about him? Jesus said: don't worry about him. You follow me! Jesus has a special path for each one of us. Today is the last ordinary day of Easter. Tomorrow is Pentecost, the birthday of the Church, when the Holy Spirit came!
family.intention: We pray for our Church as Pentecost comes, and for prisoners and all who are in chains.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we sometimes compare ourselves with our brothers, sisters or friends? How can we stop?” Then pray together: Come, Holy Spirit!

illus: An illustration

Two sisters in a Thrissur family were always being compared: one was good at mathematics, the other at music. Their grandmother kept a small framed card on the wall with the words of John 21:22: What is that to you? Follow me! When they quarrelled about who was better, she would point at the card and say: God has not given you the same road; he has given you the same Lord. Years later one became a nurse and the other a music teacher, and both say that card taught them to stop competing and start following.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call each of us by name and say: Follow me! Give us your Spirit, so that we may follow you with boldness and joy. Amen.
share: It is for the sake of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain (Acts 28:20). What hope am I ready to suffer for?
Proclaiming the kingdom of God … with all boldness and without hindrance (Acts 28:31). What stops me from speaking about Jesus?
What is that to you? Follow me! (John 21:22). Whom do I compare myself with, and what does Jesus say to me about it?
pm.resp: The upright shall behold his face.
interc: For the Church on the eve of Pentecost, that she may be renewed by the Holy Spirit.
For prisoners, especially those imprisoned for their faith, that the word of God may not be chained in them.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may be blessed in faithfulness to his covenant.
For all who feel they are not as gifted as others, that they may find joy in their own road.
For our group, that we may be found praying together with Mary when the Holy Spirit comes.
pm.close: Father, at the close of the Easter season we wait for the promise of your Son. Pour out your Spirit on us, so that we may follow Christ and bear true witness to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Eden God promised that a woman and her offspring would stand against the serpent; the Fathers saw Mary as the New Eve.
From the cross Jesus gave his mother to the beloved disciple, and through him to every disciple: Here is your mother.
Since 2018 the Church keeps the Monday after Pentecost as the memorial of Mary, Mother of the Church; Ordinary Time resumes today.
2027-05-17.action: Pray the Angelus at noon today, for the first time since Easter, and offer it for your parish.
2027-05-17.question: Have I really taken Mary into my home, as the beloved disciple did?
kidsaint: Mary, Mother of the Church

When Jesus was dying on the cross, he looked at his mother Mary and at his friend John, and said to John: here is your mother. Jesus gave his own mother to John, and to all of us! Then after Jesus went to heaven, Mary prayed with the apostles until the Holy Spirit came. That is why we call her the Mother of the Church. Lesson: Mary is your mother too; you can talk to her any time, and she will lead you to Jesus.

family.explain: When Jesus was on the cross, his mother Mary was standing close by, with his friend John. Jesus said to Mary: here is your son. And to John: here is your mother. From that day John took Mary into his home. Jesus wants us to take Mary into our home too. She is the Mother of the whole Church, our family of faith.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers, especially mothers who are sick, alone or grieving, and for our parish family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Mary feel at home in our family?” Pray the Angelus together at noon or in the evening.

illus: An illustration

In many Kerala homes, when a daughter marries and leaves for her new house, her mother gives her a small picture of the Blessed Virgin to keep in the new prayer corner. It is a way of saying: you are going far from me, but you are not going without a mother. That is what Jesus did on the cross. He was leaving his disciples, and he did not leave them orphans: before he died, he gave them his own Mother.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church, you stood by the cross and prayed with the apostles for the Spirit. Pray with us now. Amen.
share: Where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Where am I hiding from God today, and what would it mean to answer him?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). What place does Mary have in my daily life and prayer?
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with … Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). How can our group pray more faithfully together, as the first Church did?
pm.resp: Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God.
interc: For the Church, our Mother, that through Mary's prayers she may be fruitful in holiness and draw all peoples to Christ.
For the Pope and the bishops, that like the apostles in the upper room they may be united with Mary in prayer.
For mothers, especially those who suffer for their children or have lost them, that Mary may comfort them.
For those who feel orphaned or alone, that they may know they have a Mother in heaven and a family in the Church.
For our group, that as Ordinary Time begins we may live each ordinary day doing whatever Jesus tells us.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave us his Mother as he hung upon the cross. Through her prayers, make us faithful children of the Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ben Sira warns: whoever comes to serve the Lord must prepare for testing; gold is tested in the fire.
Jesus foretells his Passion and Resurrection a second time; the disciples argue about who is the greatest.
He sets a child among them: to be first, be last and servant of all; whoever welcomes a child welcomes him.
2027-05-18.action: Do one hidden act of service today for someone who has no power to repay you.
2027-05-18.question: In the trials of my life, am I clinging to the Lord or quietly drifting away?
kidsaint: St John I

John was an old and gentle pope in Rome about fifteen hundred years ago. A powerful king sent him on a long sea journey to the emperor in Constantinople. The emperor welcomed him with great honour, but when John came back, the king did not trust him and put him in prison, where he died. Lesson: being faithful to Jesus matters more than being important or comfortable.

family.explain: On the road the disciples argued about who was the most important. Jesus did not shout at them. He sat down, took a little child in his arms and said: the greatest is the one who serves everybody. In God's family the best place is not the top chair but the place where we help others.
family.intention: We pray for children who are not wanted or cared for, and for families going through a hard time.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our home or school does work that nobody notices? How can we thank or help them this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a large hospital in Thrissur, a senior nurse with thirty years of service used to arrive early on her last day of each month and clean the sluice room herself before the junior staff came in. A young nurse once asked her why someone of her rank did the dirtiest job. She smiled: when I was new, I thought being in charge meant giving orders. Then I watched our Lord wash feet. Since then I have never been ashamed of a bucket.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, servant of all, keep us steadfast in trial and humble in service. Amen.
share: My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing (Sirach 2:1). What testing am I facing now, and how is God purifying me in it?
On the way they had argued with one another who was the greatest (Mark 9:34). Where do I compete for first place in family, work or parish?
Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me (Mark 9:37). Who are the little ones I am being asked to welcome?
