In the Gospel Jesus says something hard: it is to your advantage that I go away (John 16:7). The disciples could not understand. How could losing him be good? But if he does not go, the Advocate will not come. In a few days we will celebrate his Ascension, and then Pentecost. He goes so that his Spirit can be with each of us, everywhere, even in a prison at midnight. Let us trust him in our losses, praise him in our darkness, and wait for the Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul and Silas were in jail, with their feet locked up. Did they cry? No, they sang songs to God in the middle of the night! Then God sent an earthquake and the doors opened. The jailer was so amazed that he and his family came to know Jesus. When you are sad or scared, try singing a little song to Jesus. He hears you!

homily: Dear friends, imagine Paul in Athens: a Jewish tentmaker standing before the philosophers of the most learned city in the world. What does he say? He does not mock them. He says: Athenians, I see how extremely religious you are in every way (Acts 17:22). He has seen an altar to an unknown god, and he says: what you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.

Paul shows us how to speak about Jesus to people of other faiths. First, respect. Look for the good that is already there, the search for God, the prayer, the longing. Second, start from what we share: the one Creator who gives life and breath to all, who made every nation, in whom we live and move and have our being (Acts 17:28). God is not far from each one of us.

Third, do not hide what is new. Paul ends with the Resurrection: God has raised Jesus from the dead. And some laughed. Some said: we will hear you again. Most went away. But Dionysius and a woman named Damaris and others believed. We do not measure success by the size of the crowd. Seeds sown in Athens grew into a Church.

In the Gospel Jesus says: when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). The Spirit does not give a different Gospel; he takes what belongs to Jesus and makes it clearer. In our country of many temples and many seekers, let us ask the Spirit to give us Paul's respect and Paul's courage, and to guide us, and our neighbours, into the whole truth of the risen Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul went to a big city called Athens, full of statues of gods. He saw an altar that said: to an unknown god. Paul said: I know this God! He made everything, he gives you life, and he is very close to you. His Son Jesus rose from the dead. When we talk to friends who do not know Jesus, let us be kind and polite like Paul, and tell them how good God is.

homily: Dear friends, we think of St Paul as a man without fear. Today's reading tells us otherwise. One night in Corinth the Lord speaks to him in a vision: do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you (Acts 18:9–10). The Lord would not say do not be afraid to someone who was not afraid.

Paul himself told the Corinthians later: I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling. He had been beaten in other cities, chased out at night. Now in Corinth he wondered: will it happen again? And the Lord says: I am with you, and there are many in this city who are my people.

Notice what the Lord promises and what he does not. He does not promise that nobody will make trouble. Trouble does come: Paul is dragged before the judge Gallio. But the Lord keeps his word: no one harms him. The judge refuses the case, and Paul goes on preaching. God's protection sometimes comes through strange doors, even through the indifference of a Roman official.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of a mother in labour. She has pain because her hour has come, but when the child is born she forgets the pain because of her joy. Mothers here know this better than any preacher. Jesus is speaking of his own hour, his cross. His Passion was a birth.

Today is First Friday. We look at the Heart of Jesus, opened by the soldier's spear. From it came blood and water, and from it the Church was born. That is why our joy is a joy that no one can take away: it was born from his love, and his love does not die.

So if you are afraid today, hear the Lord's word to Paul: do not be afraid; I am with you. Come to his Heart in confession and in Communion. And from today, with Mary, let us begin to pray for the Holy Spirit, who will give us courage to speak. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, even St Paul was sometimes afraid! But Jesus told him: do not be afraid, I am with you. Jesus says the same to you when you are scared.
Today is First Friday, a day to remember Jesus' Heart, full of love. Put your hand on your heart and say: Jesus, I love you too!

homily: Dear friends, today we meet a brilliant young preacher, Apollos from Alexandria. He was eloquent, he knew the Scriptures well, and he spoke about Jesus with burning enthusiasm. But there was something missing: he knew only the baptism of John.

Who noticed? Not a bishop, not an apostle, but a tentmaking couple, Priscilla and Aquila. And what did they do? They did not stand up in the synagogue and shout: you are wrong! They took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately (Acts 18:26). Probably at their own table, in their own home.

This is how Christians correct one another: privately, kindly, with the wish to help, not to win. And see the humility of Apollos: a learned man from the great city of Alexandria, he accepted teaching from two workers. Because he was humble, he became an even greater blessing to the Church.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches us to pray in his name: if you ask anything of the Father in my name, he will give it to you (John 16:23). And then he says: the Father himself loves you (John 16:27). Many of us pray as if God were an angry officer who must be persuaded. Jesus says no. The Father already loves you.

Jesus also says: I came from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and am going to the Father. Tomorrow, in India, we celebrate that return to the Father, the Ascension of the Lord.

Today is Saturday, a day dedicated to Mary. After the Ascension the apostles waited for the Holy Spirit, praying with Mary the mother of Jesus. Let us do the same: ask the Father, in Jesus' name, with Mary beside us, for the Holy Spirit. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, a clever preacher named Apollos did not know everything about Jesus. So Aquila and Priscilla invited him home and taught him kindly. We can help our friends kindly too!
Jesus says: the Father loves you! When you pray, you are talking to someone who loves you very much. Say: Father, I love you too!

homily: Dear friends, imagine Paul walking into Ephesus and meeting twelve people who say they are believers. He looks at them and asks a simple question: did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers? And they answer: no, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit (Acts 19:2).

They were good people. They had been baptized with John's baptism, a baptism of repentance. They had turned from sin. But they had stopped halfway. Paul baptized them in the name of the Lord Jesus, laid his hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came upon them. A little Pentecost in Ephesus.

Now, if Paul walked into our church this morning and asked the same question, what would we say? We would say: yes, of course, we were baptized and confirmed. But do we live like people who have received the Spirit? Do we ever pray to him? Do we ask his help before a hard decision? For many Christians, the Holy Spirit is the forgotten Person of the Trinity.

We are in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. This is the best time to get to know him. Pray every day: Come, Holy Spirit. Ask him for his gifts: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord. He is not an idea; he is a Person, and he is waiting to be asked.

In the Gospel Jesus knows that his disciples will run away that very night. Yet he says: take courage; I have conquered the world (John 16:33). The Spirit is the one who gives us that courage. The same frightened disciples, after Pentecost, would stand before rulers and say: we cannot keep from speaking.

Today we remember St John of Avila, a Spanish priest who was falsely accused and put in prison. In prison he did not grow bitter; he grew in love for Christ. He came out and became one of the great preachers of his time. That is what the Holy Spirit does. So let us ask him today: Come, Holy Spirit, and give us courage. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul met some people who had never heard of the Holy Spirit! He prayed with them, and the Holy Spirit came into their hearts.
You received the Holy Spirit when you were baptized. He is your best helper. When you are scared or need to be good, just say: Holy Spirit, help me!

homily: Dear friends, today we stand on the beach at Miletus and listen to a farewell. Paul has called the elders of Ephesus, and he speaks to them for the last time. What does he remember? Not his success, not his miracles, but this: I served the Lord with all humility and with tears (Acts 20:19).

He tells them: I did not shrink from doing anything helpful; I taught you publicly and from house to house. I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole purpose of God (Acts 20:20, 27). Paul did not give his people only the easy parts of the Gospel. He gave them all of it, because he loved them.

Then he looks ahead. He is going to Jerusalem, and he does not know exactly what will happen, only that chains are waiting. Yet he says: I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24). Paul sees his life as a race. What matters is not how long it is, but that it is finished well.

Each of us has a course to run. A mother, a farmer, a student, a priest, a sick person in bed: each has a ministry received from the Lord Jesus. The question is not whether it is easy, but whether we will finish it with faith.

In the Gospel Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and prays: Father, the hour has come. And he tells us what eternal life is: this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent (John 17:3). Eternal life is not only after death. It begins now, when we know God, not just about him, but as a friend knows a friend.

Jesus says: I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. These are Ascension words. He has gone to the Father, but he has not stopped praying for us. In these days before Pentecost, let us let him pray for us, and let us run our course to the end, with the Holy Spirit as our strength. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul had to say goodbye to his friends in Ephesus. He told them: I loved you, I taught you everything about Jesus, and I even cried for you. Now I must go where God sends me.
Jesus prayed to his Father for his friends, and he prays for you too. He wants you to know God as your best friend. Say: Jesus, I want to know you more!

homily: Dear friends, have you ever stood at a railway station or an airport to say goodbye to someone you love? Today Paul stands on the shore at Miletus with the elders of Ephesus. He knows that he will not see them again. And his last words are not about himself, but about them and about the Church: keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock (Acts 20:28).

Paul tells them why the flock is so precious. It is the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son. Every parish, every family of believers, has been bought at that price. That is why a shepherd must be watchful, and why every Christian must care for the faith of others. Paul then points to his own hands. He took nothing from them; he worked to support himself and the weak, remembering the word of the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35).

In the Gospel Jesus too is saying goodbye, and he prays for us. Holy Father, protect them in your name. I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but I ask you to protect them from the evil one (John 17:15). Jesus does not want us to run away from the office, the college, the market. He wants us there, but belonging to God. Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth (John 17:17).

The martyrs Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers who laid down their weapons for Christ, and Pancras was only a boy of about fourteen. They lived in the world, but they belonged to God, and the Father kept them faithful to the end. In these days before Pentecost, let us ask the Holy Spirit to make us holy in the truth, generous in giving, and faithful shepherds of whoever God has placed in our care. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul had to say goodbye to his friends, and they all cried and hugged. He told them: remember what Jesus said, it is better to give than to receive. Jesus also prayed for his friends that God would keep them safe from the evil one. Today, try to give something: share a toy, help at home, or say a kind word. Giving makes Jesus smile!

homily: Dear friends, imagine Paul in the barracks of Jerusalem that night. He has been beaten, arrested, shouted at in the council. He is alone. And then the Lord stood near him and said, Keep up your courage! For just as you have testified for me in Jerusalem, so you must bear witness also in Rome (Acts 23:11). The risen Jesus does not take the danger away. He stands beside his servant in it.

Why was Paul on trial? He said it himself: I am on trial concerning the hope of the resurrection of the dead (Acts 23:6). That is our hope too. Death does not have the last word. The Psalm sings it: you show me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy (Psalm 16:11). When we are afraid, we can say with the psalmist: I keep the Lord always before me; I shall not be moved.

In the Gospel, Jesus prays for us by name, so to speak: not only for these, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one (John 17:20–21). You and I were in that prayer on the night before he died. And he asks for a unity like that of the Father and the Son, so that the world may believe. Our quarrels in families and parishes are not small things; they hide Jesus from the world. Our love makes him visible.

Today we also remember Our Lady of Fatima. To three shepherd children in a time of war she asked for simple things: pray the Rosary every day, pray for sinners, pray for peace. Let us do what she asked. As we wait for Pentecost, let us gather with Mary in prayer, so that the Holy Spirit may make us one and give us courage to bear witness, in Jerusalem, in Rome, and wherever the Lord sends us. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul was in big trouble and all alone. But that night Jesus came and stood beside him and said: be brave! Jesus is beside you too when you are afraid. Jesus also prayed that all his friends would be one big loving family. And at Fatima, Mother Mary asked three children to pray the Rosary for peace. Can you say one Hail Mary for peace today?

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate an apostle who is mentioned by name only twice in the whole Bible, both times in one chapter of the Acts of the Apostles. We know almost nothing of his words or his travels. And yet Matthias is one of the twelve foundations of the Church.

The apostles had returned from the Mount of Olives and were praying in the upper room with Mary and the other women. There was an empty place. Judas, who had been one of them, had gone to his own place. Jesus had chosen twelve, for the twelve tribes of Israel. Before the Holy Spirit came, the circle had to be complete.

Peter says what kind of person is needed: one who had been with Jesus from the baptism of John to the Ascension, and who could become a witness with us to his resurrection (Acts 1:22). Not the cleverest, not the richest, not the most popular. The one who had stayed with Jesus, and had seen him alive.

Then the community did something we often forget to do: they prayed before they decided. Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen (Acts 1:24). They did not want their own choice; they wanted the Lord's. And the lot fell on Matthias. How many of our family quarrels and wrong decisions would be avoided if we prayed like this first?

In the Gospel Jesus tells us that this is how every vocation works. You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). Our faith is first of all the Lord's choice of us. And he chooses us as friends: I do not call you servants any longer, but I have called you friends. The mark of his friends is love: love one another as I have loved you.

Perhaps you feel like Matthias before that day: following Jesus quietly, never noticed, never named. Do not be discouraged. The Lord sees you. He raises the poor from the dust to make them sit with princes. Stay with him, be a witness of his resurrection where you are, and when he calls, be ready. St Matthias, pray for us, and with Mary and the apostles, let us pray: Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Matthias followed Jesus for a long, long time, but nobody wrote his name in the Gospels. He was a quiet friend of Jesus. When the apostles needed one more, they prayed, and God chose Matthias!
Jesus says to you: I chose you, and you are my friend. Even when nobody notices you, Jesus sees you. Say: Thank you, Jesus, for choosing me!

homily: Dear friends, today we come to the last page of two books. Since Easter we have been reading the Acts of the Apostles and the Gospel of John. Both end today, and both end in a surprising way: not with a full stop, but with an open door.

Acts ends in Rome. Paul is a prisoner, chained to a soldier, but he is not silent. He calls the Jewish leaders of the city his brothers, and he tells them: it is for the sake of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain (Acts 28:20). Then for two whole years he welcomed all who came to him, proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance (Acts 28:31). We do not hear how his trial ended. Luke leaves the story open, because it is not finished. We are the next chapter.

John's Gospel ends on the shore of the lake. Peter has just been told how he would die, and he looks at John and asks: Lord, what about him? How often we do the same! Why does he have it easier? Why did she get that gift and not me? Jesus answers: what is that to you? Follow me! (John 21:22). Each of us has a road. Our task is not to measure the roads of others, but to walk our own behind Jesus.

Tonight, at the Vigil of Pentecost, the Church will pray with the apostles and with Mary for the gift of the Holy Spirit. Let us bring to that prayer our chains and our comparisons. The Spirit who made Paul bold in chains and made John a true witness will make us bold and true as well. The world could not contain all the books about Jesus; let the Holy Spirit write a few more lines in our lives. Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today two books in the Bible come to their last page. In the first one, St Paul is a prisoner in Rome, but he still tells everyone about Jesus. In the second, Peter asks Jesus: what about John? And Jesus says: don't worry about him, you follow me! Jesus has a special path just for you. Tomorrow is Pentecost, the birthday of the Church! Let us say: Come, Holy Spirit!

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated Pentecost, the birthday of the Church. Today, the very next day, the Church turns to a mother. Every birth has a mother, and the Church does too. Since 2018 the Monday after Pentecost has been the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church.

The first reading takes us to the very beginning. After the first sin, God calls Adam: where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Adam hides and blames. But in the middle of that sad scene God makes a promise: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head (Genesis 3:15). Long before Bethlehem, God already had a woman and her Son in mind. The Fathers called Mary the New Eve: what Eve lost by disobedience, Mary restored by her yes.

In the Gospel we stand at the cross. Jesus is dying. And with almost his last breath, he thinks of his mother and of his friend. Woman, here is your son. Here is your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home (John 19:26–27). The disciple has no name in the Gospel, so that you can put your name there. Jesus gives his Mother to you. And then from his pierced side flow blood and water, the sacraments by which the Church is born and fed. Mary was there.

And after the Ascension, Mary was in the upper room, praying with the apostles until the Spirit came (Acts 1:14). She is the Mother who stays with the Church in prayer. Today Ordinary Time begins again. Ordinary days, ordinary work, ordinary family life. Let us take Mary into our homes for these ordinary days, as John did. At noon today we pray the Angelus again; let us pray it with love. And let us listen to her one instruction, given at Cana: do whatever he tells you. Holy Mary, Mother of the Church, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was on the cross, his mother Mary was standing near him with his friend John. Jesus said to John: here is your mother! Jesus gave his own Mummy to John, and to you and me! Mary is the Mother of the whole Church. Whenever you are sad or scared, you can talk to her, and she will take you to Jesus. Let us say: Holy Mary, my Mother, pray for me!

homily: Dear friends, Pentecost is over and the ordinary weeks of the year have begun again. The first word the Church gives us is not a soft one. My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing (Sirach 2:1). Some people imagine that once we give our lives to God, everything will go smoothly. Ben Sira, a wise teacher of Jerusalem, says the opposite: get ready.

But he gives us a beautiful picture. Gold is tested in the fire (Sirach 2:5). A goldsmith in Thrissur or Kozhikode heats the gold not to spoil it but to burn away what is not gold. When the fire of trouble comes, God is not destroying us. He is purifying us. And Ben Sira asks: has anyone trusted in the Lord and been disappointed? Look back at your own life, and the lives of your parents. God has never failed those who clung to him.

In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples for the second time that he will be betrayed, killed and raised. And what are they talking about on the road? Who is the greatest (Mark 9:34). It is almost funny, and it is very human. We do the same: in families, in offices, even in parish committees. Jesus does not shout. He sits down, takes a little child in his arms, and says: whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.

Today we remember St John I, an old pope who was sent on a hard journey, then thrown into prison by a king who did not trust him, where he died. He did not choose the first place. He accepted the fire and was found to be pure gold. Let us ask for his courage: to cling to the Lord in trial, and to spend our lives serving the little ones. Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples once had a big argument: who is the most important? Jesus took a small child, maybe as small as you, held the child in his arms and said: if you want to be first, help everybody. So in God's eyes the most important person is the one who serves. Can you help someone today without being asked?

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira tells us that Wisdom is like a mother who teaches her children. Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early morning are filled with joy (Sirach 4:12). Notice: from early morning. The wise person does not wait until the day is spoiled to look for God.

But Wisdom is not a soft teacher. At first she will walk with them on tortuous paths; she will bring fear and dread upon them (Sirach 4:17). She tests us before she trusts us. Every student who has struggled with mathematics, every apprentice who has spent months only sweeping the workshop, knows this. Then, Ben Sira says, she comes straight back and gladdens us, and reveals her secrets. For us Christians this Wisdom has a face: Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God.

In the Gospel John is proud of himself. We saw a man casting out demons in your name, and we stopped him, because he was not following us. Not following us. How easily we say this too: not our parish, not our association, not our Church. Jesus answers: do not stop him. Whoever is not against us is for us (Mark 9:40).

This does not mean that all ways are the same, or that the Church does not matter. It means that we never become jealous of God's goodness. Wherever the sick are healed, the poor are fed and the name of Jesus is honoured, we rejoice, and we pray that all may come to the fullness of his truth and to the unity he prayed for. Let us ask Wisdom to make our hearts as wide as the heart of Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, once the disciples saw a man doing good things in Jesus' name. But he was not in their group, so they told him to stop! Jesus said: do not stop him. Jesus is happy whenever someone does good. So when another child does something kind, even if they are not your friend, you can be happy too and say: thank you, God!

homily: Dear friends, there is one word the devil loves: tomorrow. I will pray tomorrow. I will go to confession next month. I will forgive my brother after he apologises. Ben Sira knew this temptation well, and he says today: do not delay to turn back to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day (Sirach 5:7).

He also warns us against sentences we say inside. I have enough. Who can control me? I sinned and nothing happened. God is merciful, he will forgive anything. Yes, God is merciful, wonderfully merciful. But his mercy is meant to lead us to repentance, not to give us permission to add sin to sin.

In the Gospel Jesus uses very strong words. If your hand, your foot, your eye causes you to sin, cut it off. He does not want us to harm our bodies. He wants us to be serious. If a mobile phone, a bottle, a bad friendship or a habit keeps pulling me into sin, I must cut it off decisively. Nothing is worth more than eternal life.

But Jesus also says something very gentle: whoever gives you a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ will by no means lose the reward (Mark 9:41). Today we remember St Bernardine of Siena, who preached conversion across Italy and taught people to love the Holy Name of Jesus. Let us take his advice: say the name of Jesus often, turn to him today, not tomorrow, and be at peace with one another. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes we say: I will say sorry tomorrow, I will clean my room later, I will pray next time. The Bible says: do not wait! Turn to God today. And Jesus says that even giving a cup of water to someone with love makes God happy. Can you say sorry and do a small kindness today?

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira says something we all know from experience. When you are doing well, many people are your friends. But there are friends who sit at your table, but they will not stand by you in time of trouble (Sirach 6:10). When the hospital bill comes, or the business fails, the table empties.

And then he praises the true friend: faithful friends are a sturdy shelter: whoever finds one has found a treasure (Sirach 6:14). A faithful friend is life-saving medicine. Where do we find such friends? Ben Sira answers: those who fear the Lord will find them. When God is at the centre, friendship becomes faithful.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of the closest friendship of all, marriage. The Pharisees want to discuss when divorce is allowed. Jesus takes them back to the beginning: God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate (Mark 10:9). This is not a heavy rule; it is God's dream for love. And Christ gives the grace to live it. To those who are hurting from broken marriages, the Church does not close the door; she walks with them.

Today we remember St Christopher Magallanes, a parish priest in Mexico, arrested a hundred years ago today on his way to celebrate Mass, and shot four days later. He forgave his killers and prayed that his blood would bring peace to his country. He was a faithful friend of Jesus to the end. Let us be faithful friends, faithful husbands and wives, and faithful disciples. Amen.
kids: Children, a true friend is someone who stays with you when you are sad, not only when you have sweets to share! Jesus is that kind of friend. He also says that when a mother and father get married, God joins them together. Let us pray for our parents today and be good friends to everyone.

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira reminds us of two truths today. First, we are dust: the Lord created human beings out of earth, and makes them return to it again (Sirach 17:1). Second, we are precious: he made them in his own image. He gave us eyes, ears, a tongue and a mind, so that we might praise him and love our neighbour.

If we forget that we are dust, we become proud. If we forget that we are made in his image, we despair. The Psalm holds both together: as a father has compassion for his children, so the Lord has compassion for those who fear him. He knows how we were made; he remembers that we are dust (Psalm 103:13–14). Our weakness does not surprise God.

In the Gospel mothers bring their little ones to Jesus, and the disciples try to send them away. Jesus is indignant. Let the little children come to me; do not stop them; for it is to such as these that the kingdom of God belongs (Mark 10:14). Children do not earn gifts; they receive them. This is how we must come to God: not with a list of our achievements, but with open hands.

Today many of us remember St Rita of Cascia, a wife and mother who suffered a hard marriage and the loss of her husband and sons, and who answered violence with forgiveness. She is called the saint of impossible causes because she trusted God like a child even when everything seemed lost. Tomorrow we celebrate the Most Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who has made us his children. Let us come to him as children. Amen.
kids: Children, once mothers brought their babies and little children to Jesus, but the disciples said: go away! Jesus was not happy with the disciples. He said: let the children come to me! Then he hugged them and blessed them. Jesus loves you very much and always has time for you. You can talk to him anytime!

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira gives us good news today. Yet to those who repent he grants a return, and he encourages those who are losing hope (Sirach 17:24). However far we have wandered, the road back to God is not closed. He does not wait with folded arms; he comes to meet those who are losing courage.

The Psalm tells us what it feels like to keep sin hidden: while I kept silence, my body wasted away. And what happens when we confess: I acknowledged my sin to you, and you forgave the guilt of my sin (Psalm 32:3, 5). The sacrament of Reconciliation is the place where this happens for us.

In the Gospel a good man runs to Jesus and kneels. He has kept the commandments since his youth. And Mark says: Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21). Before any challenge, there is love. Then Jesus asks for the one thing he lacked: sell what you own, give to the poor, and come, follow me. The man went away grieving, for he had many possessions. His things owned him.

Most of us are not asked to sell everything. But all of us are asked: is there anything I hold more tightly than Jesus? Money, a house, a career, a relationship, my own plans? If we feel it is impossible to let go, Jesus answers: for mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible (Mark 10:27). Today many honour Mary, Help of Christians. Let us ask her help to let go and follow her Son, and let us pray for our brothers and sisters in China. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus looked at him with love and said: share your things with the poor and come with me. But the man went away sad, because he loved his things too much. Jesus wants us to love him more than toys, games or phones. Can you share something with someone today?

homily: Dear friends, the wise man Ben Sira lived at a time when the Temple in Jerusalem was full of sacrifices: lambs, bulls, flour, oil. He loved the Temple. But he tells us that there are other sacrifices too. The one who returns a kindness offers choice flour, and one who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering (Sirach 35:3–4). A kind word to a neighbour, a coin to a beggar, a commandment kept when it is hard: all of these are laid on God's altar.

Then he says something very human: with every gift show a cheerful face (Sirach 35:11). We all know people who give, but with a long face, so that everyone knows how much it cost them. Ben Sira says: do not give like that. Give to the Most High as he has given to you. God did not give us life and family and daily bread with a long face. He gave gladly. Our giving should look like his.

And he warns us: do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it (Sirach 35:14). Sometimes we treat God like an officer who must be pleased before he signs our paper. I will give this candle, this offering, if you give me that job. God is not like that. We give because he has already given, not to buy his favour.

In the Gospel Peter asks the question we all ask quietly: Look, we have left everything and followed you. What will we get? Jesus answers: a hundredfold now in this age, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life (Mark 10:30). He does not hide the cost. But he promises that nobody who gives to him will be the loser. Today, let us give something gladly, and trust the God who repays sevenfold and a hundredfold. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine your friend gives you a present but makes a grumpy face while giving it. Would you be happy? A wise man in the Bible says: when you give something to God, give it with a smiling face! Jesus told his friends: if you give up something for me, I will give you back a hundred times more. God is the most generous Giver of all. Let us give to him with a big smile!

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira prays for his small, suffering people, and his prayer is wider than his own nation. As you have used us to show your holiness to them, he prays, so use them to show your glory to us. Then they will know, as we have known, that there is no God but you, O Lord (Sirach 36:4–5). He wants the whole world to know the true God. That is still the prayer of the Church: that all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord.

In the Gospel Jesus is walking ahead on the road to Jerusalem. He tells the Twelve for the third time that he will suffer, die and rise. And right then James and John come and ask for the best seats: one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory (Mark 10:37). We smile at them. But how often we do the same: we follow Jesus, and quietly we hope for a little honour, a good name, a front seat.

Jesus answers gently: are you able to drink the cup that I drink? The cup is his suffering, his self-giving. Then he calls all twelve together and says: whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant. For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Mark 10:43, 45). In his kingdom, the chair of honour is a servant's stool.

St Philip Neri understood this. In Rome, a city full of honours and titles, he refused to become a cardinal. He spent his days in the confessional, in the hospitals, with poor young men. And he did it with joy, with jokes, with music. He showed that serving is not a sad duty; it is the joy of the Holy Spirit. Let us ask for that joy today, and look for one small chance to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, two of Jesus' friends wanted the best chairs, right next to Jesus! Jesus said: in my kingdom the most important person is the one who helps others. St Philip Neri was like that. He helped poor people and sick people, and he was always laughing and joking. Today, can you help someone at home, and do it with a big smile, like St Philip?

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira looks at the world and cannot stop praising. The sun looks down on everything with its light, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory (Sirach 42:16). He sees that God made all things by his word, that nothing is incomplete, that each thing completes the other. And he asks a beautiful question: who could ever tire of seeing his glory? (Sirach 42:25).

But in the Gospel there is a man who cannot see any of it. Bartimaeus is blind. He sits by the road outside Jericho, begging. He has never seen the sun or the trees or the faces of the people who pass by. But he hears that Jesus is passing, and he shouts: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me! (Mark 10:47).

People tell him to be quiet. Do not disturb the Master. But he cries out even more loudly. And then the most wonderful line: Jesus stood still. The one through whom the heavens were made stops for a blind beggar. He calls him. And Bartimaeus throws off his cloak, jumps up and comes to Jesus. That cloak was probably all he owned. He leaves it behind because he has found something better.

Jesus asks him: what do you want me to do for you? He says: my teacher, let me see again. Go; your faith has made you well. And Bartimaeus does not go home. He follows Jesus on the way (Mark 10:52). This is our story too. We are often blind to God's glory and to our neighbour's need. Let us cry out today: Jesus, have mercy on me. Let us throw off whatever holds us back, ask him to open our eyes, and then follow him. Amen.
kids: Children, close your eyes for a moment. Now you cannot see anything! That is how Bartimaeus lived every day. But when he heard that Jesus was coming, he shouted as loudly as he could: Jesus, help me! People told him to be quiet, but he shouted even louder. Jesus stopped, called him, and healed his eyes. Now open your eyes! Let us thank God for our eyes and for all the beautiful things we can see.

homily: Dear friends, Ben Sira praises the great heroes of Israel's history. But he also remembers the forgotten ones: of others there is no memory. And he says: these also were godly men, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten (Sirach 44:9–10). God does not forget. The grandmother who prayed the rosary every evening, the father who worked honestly all his life: they are not in the history books, but they are in God's book, and their goodness lives in us.

In the Gospel Jesus is hungry and sees a fig tree full of leaves. From a distance it looks wonderful. But when he comes close he finds nothing but leaves (Mark 11:13). Then he goes into the Temple and finds it busy with buying and selling. He drives out the traders and says: my house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations (Mark 11:17). The fig tree is a picture: much activity, many leaves, but no fruit.

This is a warning for us, not for others. A parish can be very busy, with feasts, programmes, collections and meetings, and still have little real prayer. A Christian can say many prayers and still have a hard heart. Jesus is looking for fruit. And he tells us what fruit he wants: have faith in God (Mark 11:22). Trust that he hears. Pray with confidence.

And then he says the most important thing: whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you (Mark 11:25). The best fruit of prayer is a forgiving heart. Today let us thank God for the forgotten saints in our families, and let us bring to him one person we need to forgive. Then our hearts will be a house of prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once saw a tree with lots of green leaves, but when he looked for fruit, there was none! Then he went to God's house, the Temple, and people were busy buying and selling instead of praying. Jesus said: God's house is for praying! He also said: when you pray, forgive anyone who has hurt you. Tonight before you pray, forgive your brother, your sister or your friend. That is a beautiful fruit for Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, at the end of his long book Ben Sira tells us his own story. While I was still young, before I went on my travels, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. Before the temple I asked for her, and I will search for her until the end (Sirach 51:13–14). He did not find wisdom first in books. He found her on his knees.

He also says that wisdom grew in him slowly, like grapes on a vine, from the first blossom to the ripening grape. And it took effort: my soul grappled with wisdom. And it needed a clean heart: in purity I found her (Sirach 51:20). Many children will soon go back to school. Let us pray that they become not only clever but wise, and that they learn, like Ben Sira, to ask God for wisdom.

In the Gospel the leaders ask Jesus: by what authority are you doing these things? Jesus asks them about John the Baptist: was his baptism from heaven or of human origin? They do not ask what is true. They ask what is safe. If we say this, he will say that; if we say that, the crowd will be angry. So they answer: we do not know (Mark 11:33). The same temptation lives in us: to decide what is true by what others will think.

Jesus' authority comes from his Father, and we receive it with an open heart. St Paul VI, whom we may remember today, held great authority as pope. But he laid down the papal crown for the poor and came to India to honour Jesus in the Eucharist. He taught that people listen to witnesses more than to teachers. Let us ask today for wisdom, for an honest heart, and for the courage to be witnesses of the truth. Amen.
kids: Children, a wise man in the Bible says: when I was young, I prayed and asked God to make me wise. Being wise means knowing what is good and choosing it. The psalm says God's words are sweeter than honey! Soon school will begin. Every morning, before you study, say a little prayer: Jesus, help me to learn, and make me wise and good.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we close the month of May with a beautiful journey. A young woman from Nazareth, who has just said yes to God, sets out on foot over the hills. She is carrying the Son of God within her. Nobody can see him yet. But wherever she goes, he goes.

The prophet Zephaniah had sung long before: sing aloud, O daughter Zion! The Lord, your God, is in your midst (Zephaniah 3:14, 17). The Hebrew words can mean in your womb. In Mary the prophecy is fulfilled literally. God is not only near his people; he is living inside a young girl from a small village. That is why Mary's whole life is joy.

And what does she do with this joy? St Luke says: Mary set out and went with haste (Luke 1:39). She does not stay at home thinking about her privilege. She hears that her old relative Elizabeth is expecting a baby, and she goes to help. The first thing Mary does with Jesus is to carry him to someone in need. That is the pattern for every Christian: the one who receives Jesus goes out to serve.

When Mary greets her, Elizabeth's child leaps for joy, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. She cries out: blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me? (Luke 1:42–43). Every time we pray the Hail Mary, we repeat Elizabeth's words. And she adds: blessed is she who believed. Mary's greatness is first her faith.

Then Mary sings: my soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior (Luke 1:46–47). She sings of a God who looks at the lowly, who brings down the powerful and lifts up the humble, who fills the hungry with good things. Mary is not proud. She is happy because God is great and God is good to the poor. If we want to honour Mary, we must also care for the lowly and the hungry.

Today let us thank Mary for this month of May, for every Rosary prayed in our homes. And let us ask her for her haste: when we see someone in need, let us not delay. Let us visit the sick, the old, the lonely, the expectant mother. Let us carry Jesus to them, as Mary did. And then, with her, our souls too will magnify the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, after the angel told Mary she would be the mother of Jesus, she heard that her cousin Elizabeth was going to have a baby too. Did Mary say, I am too important now? No! She ran over the hills to help Elizabeth. And when Mary said hello, the baby inside Elizabeth jumped for joy, because baby Jesus was inside Mary!
Today is the last day of May, Mary's month. Let us be like Mary. Is there someone at home you can help today, quickly and with a smile? Then you are bringing Jesus to them, just like Mary did.

intro: Theme: “I have called you friends.”
A Gentile Pentecost, the God who is love, the measure of the Cross, and the friendship of Christ.

sub: Stand up; I am only a mortal.
q: For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who is not partial and takes no bribe,
Then Peter began to speak to them: “I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
points.apply: Notice this week one person you keep at a distance because of their background, and take one step towards them.

sub: Not that God has love: God is love.
Our love is the fruit, not the root.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
points.apply: Each morning this week, before you ask God for anything, thank him for loving you first.

sub: Laying down one's life in small things.
q: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it.
No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.
points.apply: Choose one daily sacrifice for someone in your home this week, and offer it quietly to Jesus.

sub: Abraham and Moses, friends of God.
Chosen to bear fruit that lasts.
q: Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.

I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament or with the Gospel this week, speaking to Jesus as to a friend.

concl: At Caesarea God showed that his love has no borders; in the First Letter of John he showed that love is his very being.
In the Gospel Jesus makes us his friends and sends us out to love as he has loved: this is the fruit that lasts.
2027-05-02.resolve: Love one person this week as Jesus loves you: first, without waiting to be repaid, and at a cost.

intro: Theme: “Your pain will turn into joy.”
Paul the tentmaker, a door kept open next to the synagogue, and the little while in which the Church waits for her Lord.

points.h: Because he was of the same trade
sub: A Jewish couple expelled from Rome.
A workshop that became a chapel.
Work that does not burden others.
q: The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
You remember our labor and toil, brothers and sisters; we worked night and day, so that we might not burden any of you while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
points.apply: Before starting work each day this week, make the sign of the cross and offer the work to Christ by name.

sub: Not walking away, but staying near.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
Crispus, the official of the synagogue, became a believer in the Lord, together with all his household; and many of the Corinthians who heard Paul became believers and were baptized.
points.apply: Pray every day this week for one person who has rejected your faith, and do them one quiet kindness.

sub: Pain that is turned, not thrown away.
q: For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
Very truly, I tell you, you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice; you will have pain, but your pain will turn into joy.
points.apply: Bring one present sorrow to the Lord in the Blessed Sacrament this week and leave it with him.

concl: Paul preached Christ from a workshop, kept his door open to those who opposed him, and saw a synagogue official come to faith.
We live in the Church's little while between the Ascension and the Lord's return; offered to him, our work becomes witness and our pain becomes joy.
2027-05-06.resolve: Offer your work to Christ each morning this week, and give him one sorrow to turn into joy.

intro: Theme: “The Lord worked with them.”
The Ascension as the beginning of the Church's mission: a question from heaven, a King enthroned, a Head joined to his Body, and a Lord who works with his witnesses.

points.h: Why do you stand looking up?
q: As they continued walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah ascended in a whirlwind into heaven.
They said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.”
points.apply: This week, after each time of prayer, ask: Lord, where are you sending me today? and do one thing in answer.

sub: Our nature in the glory of God.
q: The Lord says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
God put this power to work in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places,
points.apply: Pray slowly each night this week the line of the Creed: he ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father, and thank him for interceding for you.

points.h: Head over all things for the church
sub: The eyes of the heart enlightened.
The Head in heaven, the Body on earth.
Where the Head has gone, the Body follows.
q: To him was given dominion and glory and kingship, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, and his kingship is one that shall never be destroyed.
And he has put all things under his feet and has made him the head over all things for the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.
points.apply: Take one practical step to serve your parish, the Body of Christ, this week: a ministry, a visit, a contribution of time.

sub: The ends of the earth in our pockets.
The Lord who works with us.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: On this World Communications Day, share one message of hope or a Gospel verse, and decide not to forward anything untrue or unkind.

concl: The Ascension is not Jesus going away but Jesus going ahead: our human nature is seated in the glory of God, and the Head draws the Body after him.
Seated at the right hand of the Father, the Lord works with his witnesses everywhere; with Mary we wait for the Spirit, and then we go into all the world.
2027-05-09.resolve: Lift up your heart each morning this week, and go out each day to bear one witness to the risen and ascended Lord.

intro: Theme: “Lord, send forth your Spirit, and renew the face of the earth.”
Pentecost: the wind and fire of Acts 2, the gifts of 1 Corinthians 12, and the breath of the risen Christ on Easter evening.

q: I will put my spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you on your own soil; then you shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken and will act, says the Lord.
And suddenly from heaven there came a sound like the rush of a violent wind, and it filled the entire house where they were sitting.
points.apply: Pray each morning this week: Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart; and ask for the courage to speak of Jesus once each day.

q: Therefore it was called Babel, because there the Lord confused the language of all the earth; and from there the Lord scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.
And at this sound the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in the native language of each.
points.apply: Reach out this week to someone of another language or background in your parish or workplace, and make them feel at home.

points.h: Varieties of gifts, the same Spirit
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit;
points.apply: Name one gift you have received and offer it to your parish this month: in the choir, catechism, care for the sick or the poor.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Go to confession before the end of this month, and forgive one person from your heart.

concl: Pentecost fulfils Easter: the risen Christ pours out the Spirit who makes the Church one, holy and sent.
The same Spirit who came upon Mary and the apostles lives in us by Baptism and Confirmation, gives each of us gifts, and breathes forgiveness into the world.
2027-05-16.resolve: Pray the Sequence Come, Holy Spirit each day this week, and put one gift of the Spirit to work for the common good.

intro: Theme: “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”
The God of Israel who speaks and saves, the one God besides whom there is no other, the Spirit who makes us children, and the mission given in the one Name.

points.h: Has anything so great ever happened?
sub: Ask from one end of heaven to the other.
The voice out of the fire.
A God who chooses and rescues.
q: has anything so great as this ever happened or has its like ever been heard of?
No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.
points.apply: Write down three great things God has done in your life and thank him for each before Sunday ends.

sub: Israel's confession of the one God.
One God revealed in his inner life.
q: So acknowledge today and take to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly once this week at home, pausing on each article about the Father, the Son and the Spirit.

q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.

For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received a spirit of adoption. When we cry, “Abba! Father!” it is that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with the word “Abba” and a moment of trust.

sub: Worship and doubt on the mountain.
q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Find the date of your Baptism, and invite one person who is searching to come with you to Mass.

concl: The Trinity is not a riddle but the life of the one God, revealed in history and opened to us in Christ.
Baptised in the one Name, we are children of the Father, brothers and sisters of the Son and temples of the Spirit, sent to all nations with the Lord who is with us always.
2027-05-23.resolve: Make the sign of the cross slowly and with love every time you pray this week, and renew your baptismal promises on Sunday evening.

intro: Theme: “Take; this is my body.”
The blood of the covenant at Sinai, the blood of Christ that purifies the conscience, and the gift of the upper room carried into our streets.

sub: Blood on altar and people: one family.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
He said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.”
points.apply: At the consecration this week, when the chalice is raised, say inwardly: Lord, by your blood I belong to your family.

points.h: How much more the blood of Christ
sub: The high priest and the Holy of Holies.
Once for all, with his own blood.
q: For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you for making atonement for your lives on the altar;
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to worship the living God!
points.apply: Make a good confession before you next receive Communion if you are aware of serious sin, so that the Lord may purify your conscience.

q: What shall I return to the Lord for all his bounty to me? I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord,
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
points.apply: Stay at least two minutes in silent thanksgiving after every Holy Communion this month.

sub: The hymn and the Mount of Olives.
q: I will pay my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people,
Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.
points.apply: After the procession, share a meal or some food this week with a family or person in need, so that the Bread of Life becomes bread shared.

concl: At Sinai the blood of the covenant made Israel God's family; on the cross and at the altar the blood of Christ seals the new and eternal covenant.
In the Eucharist Jesus gives us his true Body and Blood; we adore him, receive him, and go out to become his body for the world.
2027-05-30.resolve: Make one visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week and stay in thanksgiving after every Communion.

intro: Theme: “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
Doors closed by the Spirit, a cry for help, the cost of discipleship, and the carpenter of Nazareth.

q: The human mind plans the way, but the Lord directs the steps.
When they had come opposite Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them;
points.apply: Bring one disappointment of this year to the Lord in prayer and ask, not why, but where: where are you leading me now?

q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
During the night Paul had a vision: there stood a man of Macedonia pleading with him and saying, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
points.apply: Listen this week for one person's plea for help that you have been ignoring, and answer it.

q: More in number than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause
Remember the word that I said to you, ‘Servants are not greater than their master.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.
points.apply: Pray by name for one persecuted Christian community today, and do not be ashamed to make the sign of the cross in public.

sub: May Day and the month of Mary.
q: The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
Whatever your task, put yourselves into it, as done for the Lord and not for your masters,
points.apply: Begin each working day this week with a short offering: Lord, I do this work for you; St Joseph, pray for me.

concl: The Spirit who closed two doors opened a third, and the Gospel crossed the sea in answer to a cry for help.
The disciple will share the Master's rejection, but also his fruitfulness; and with St Joseph and the Blessed Virgin Mary, our daily work becomes part of that mission.
2027-05-01.resolve: Offer your work to God each morning this May and pray one decade of the Rosary each evening.

intro: Theme: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
Two apostles: Philip who asked to see the Father, and James who saw the risen Lord.

points.h: What I in turn had received
q: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles. Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me.
points.apply: Pray the Apostles' Creed slowly each day this week, pausing at “rose again on the third day.”

points.h: Their voice goes out through all the earth
sub: Paul applies it to the apostles.
q: There is no speech, nor are there words; their voice is not heard; yet their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!
points.apply: Thank God by name this week for the missionaries, priests and catechists who brought the faith to your family.

q: Moses said, “Show me your glory, I pray.”
Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied.”
points.apply: Bring your deepest question about God to Jesus in prayer this week, honestly, as Philip did.

sub: Doers of the word, like James.
q: “Come,” my heart says, “seek his face!” Your face, Lord, do I seek.
Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you all this time, Philip, and you still do not know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”
points.apply: Do one concrete work of mercy this week as a “doer of the word,” and invite one person to “come and see.”

concl: The faith of the Church rests on the testimony of apostles like James, who saw the risen Lord, and their voice still goes out through all the earth.
In Jesus, as Philip learned, we see the Father; and like James we are called to show that faith in deeds.
2027-05-03.resolve: This week, say “come and see” to one person, and do one work of mercy in the name of Jesus.

intro: Theme: “If I go, I will send him to you.”
Praise at midnight, a jailer's question, and the gift that comes through the Lord's going away.

q: By day the Lord commands his steadfast love, and at night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
points.apply: Learn one short hymn or psalm verse by heart this week and use it whenever you feel low.

points.h: What must I do to be saved?
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
They answered, “Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
points.apply: Reach out this week to someone who seems close to despair, and stay with them as Paul stayed with the jailer.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you;
Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Begin today to pray each evening, until Pentecost: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.

concl: Paul and Silas sang in the dark, and the Spirit turned a prison into a place of Baptism.
The Lord who goes to the Father sends the Advocate, so that he may be with us everywhere, even at midnight.
2027-05-04.resolve: Praise God in one difficulty each day this week, and pray for the Holy Spirit every evening.

intro: Theme: “He will guide you into all the truth.”
Paul at the Areopagus: respect, a shared search, the Resurrection, and the Spirit of truth.

q: Truly, you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.

For as I went through the city and looked carefully at the objects of your worship, I found among them an altar with the inscription, ‘To an unknown god.’ What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.
points.apply: Learn one thing this week about the faith of a neighbour of another religion, and listen without arguing.

points.h: Not far from each one of us
sub: Life and breath and all things.
q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart,
so that they would search for God and perhaps grope for him and find him, though indeed he is not far from each one of us.
points.apply: Take a few moments each day this week simply to be aware that you live and move and have your being in God.

q: For from the greatness and beauty of created things comes a corresponding perception of their Creator.
But some of them joined him and became believers, including Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
points.apply: Do not give up on someone who once laughed at your faith; pray for them by name this week.

sub: Many things they cannot bear now.
The Spirit takes what is Christ's.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak on his own, but will speak whatever he hears, and he will declare to you the things that are to come.
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Catechism each day until Pentecost, asking the Spirit of truth to guide you.

concl: At Athens Paul showed how to proclaim Christ with respect for the search of others and without hiding the Resurrection.
The Spirit of truth continues that work in the Church, leading us and every people deeper into the one truth that is Christ.
2027-05-05.resolve: Pray each day until Pentecost: Come, Spirit of truth, and guide me and my neighbours into all the truth.

intro: Theme: “No one will take your joy from you.”
The Lord's word to a fearful apostle, a judge who opened a door without knowing it, and the labour of the cross that gives birth to joy.

points.h: Do not be afraid, but speak
sub: Many in this city are my people.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.

One night the Lord said to Paul in a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, for there are many in this city who are my people.”
points.apply: Speak one word of faith this week that you have been holding back out of fear.

sub: A judge who would not judge.
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one time he protected you through people who did not even know they were helping.

sub: The pierced Heart and the birth of the Church.
A joy that cannot be taken.
q: Shall I open the womb and not deliver? says the Lord; shall I, the one who delivers, shut the womb? says your God.
When a woman is in labor, she has pain, because her hour has come. But when her child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy of having brought a human being into the world.
points.apply: Consecrate your family to the Sacred Heart this First Friday and pray the novena to the Holy Spirit each day until Pentecost.

concl: The Lord does not always remove danger, but he removes fear by his presence: I am with you.
The cross was a labour of love; from the pierced Heart of Jesus the Church was born, and with her a joy that no one can take away.
2027-05-07.resolve: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit today, and pray it with Mary every day until Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “The Father himself loves you.”
A missionary who goes back to strengthen, a couple who correct with love, and the Son who teaches us to ask in his name as he returns to the Father.

q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
After spending some time there he departed and went from place to place through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
points.apply: This week visit or call one person whose faith has grown weak, only to encourage them.

sub: Apollos: a gift, a fire and a gap.
Correction at the table, not from the pew.
q: Give instruction to the wise, and they will become wiser still; teach the righteous and they will gain in learning.
He began to speak boldly in the synagogue; but when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the Way of God to him more accurately.
points.apply: If you must correct someone this week, do it privately and kindly; and when you are corrected, say thank you.

sub: From the Father, to the Father.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
points.apply: Begin your prayers this week with the words: Father, you love me; in the name of Jesus I ask...

concl: Paul strengthened the disciples, Priscilla and Aquila taught Apollos with love, and Apollos humbly learned: the Gospel is handed on in a chain of humble service.
Jesus, returning to the Father, teaches us to pray in his name to a Father who already loves us; with Mary we ask for the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-08.resolve: Encourage one tired believer this week, and pray every day: Father, in Jesus' name, send us your Spirit.

intro: Theme: “Take courage; I have conquered the world!”
Disciples who had not heard of the Holy Spirit, the laying on of hands, and the courage that comes from Christ's victory.

points.h: We have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit
sub: The forgotten Person of the Trinity.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” They replied, “No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
points.apply: Pray each day this week the prayer “Come, Holy Spirit,” and speak to him as a Person, not an idea.

points.h: Paul laid his hands on them
sub: Baptism in the name of Jesus.
q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!”
When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied
points.apply: Thank God for your Confirmation, and pray this week for one young person preparing for it.

q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!
points.apply: Face one fear or difficulty this week in the name of Jesus, asking the Spirit for the gift of fortitude.

concl: Like the disciples at Ephesus, we need more than a beginning; we need the Holy Spirit, given in Baptism and Confirmation and renewed in prayer.
Christ has already conquered the world; in him we have peace, and through his Spirit, the courage of St John of Avila and of all the saints.
2027-05-10.resolve: Ask the Holy Spirit each day until Pentecost for one of his seven gifts.

intro: Theme: “This is eternal life, that they may know you.”
Paul's farewell at Miletus, a life run to the finish, and the prayer of Jesus for his own as he goes to the Father.

points.h: Serving the Lord with humility and tears
sub: Publicly and from house to house.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
I did not shrink from doing anything helpful, proclaiming the message to you and teaching you publicly and from house to house,
points.apply: Visit or call one family of your parish or neighbourhood this week, simply to share faith and friendship.

points.h: If only I may finish my course
sub: A race run to the end.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
But I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the good news of God’s grace.
points.apply: Name the ministry the Lord has given you in your present state of life, and finish one neglected part of it this week.

q: but let those who boast boast in this, that they understand and know me, that I am the Lord; I act with steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the earth, for in these things I delight, says the Lord.
And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
points.apply: Read John 17 slowly once this week, and let Jesus pray for you.

concl: Paul, leaving Ephesus, gave his people all of the Gospel with humility and tears, and walked towards chains wanting only to finish his course.
Jesus, going to the Father, prays for us who remain in the world; eternal life begins now, in knowing and loving the Father and the Son through the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-11.resolve: Finish one neglected duty this week as an offering to the Lord, and pray John 17 slowly before Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.”
Two farewells: Paul on the shore at Miletus, and Jesus at the Last Supper praying for his own.

sub: Wolves and the word of grace.
q: For thus says the Lord God: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.
Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.
points.apply: This week, pray each day for your parish priest and your bishop by name, and do one thing to help the faith of someone in your care.

sub: A saying of the Lord kept by Paul.
q: A generous person will be enriched, and one who gives water will get water.
In all this I have given you an example that by such work we must support the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
points.apply: Choose one person who cannot repay you, and give them your time or help before Sunday.

sub: Not taken out of the world.
Holy and sent, like the martyrs.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
points.apply: Until Pentecost, read a few verses of the Gospel each morning before you go out into the world, and ask: Lord, make me holy in your truth today.

concl: Paul's farewell and the prayer of Jesus tell us the same thing: the Church belongs to God, bought by the blood of Christ and kept by the Father's name.
We are left in the world, not to be swallowed by it, but to be holy in the truth and sent, as the martyrs were.
2027-05-12.resolve: Pray each day until Pentecost: Holy Father, keep me in your name; Come, Holy Spirit.

intro: Theme: “That they may all be one.”
The Lord who stands by Paul in the night, the hope of the resurrection, and the prayer of Jesus for us, with Our Lady of Fatima.

q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
That night the Lord stood near him and said, “Keep up your courage! For just as you have testified for me in Jerusalem, so you must bear witness also in Rome.”
points.apply: Write down the fear that weighs on you most, and each night this week hand it to the Lord with the words: Keep up my courage, Lord.

q: For you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.
Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I am on trial concerning the hope of the resurrection of the dead.
points.apply: Visit or phone someone who is grieving this week, and share with them the hope of the resurrection.

points.h: That they may all be one
sub: Unity in the life of the Trinity.
Mary at Fatima: prayer and peace.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Take one step towards reconciliation in your family or parish before Pentecost, and pray a decade of the Rosary for the unity of Christians.

concl: The risen Lord stands near his witnesses in the night and sends them on.
He prayed for us that we may be one, so that the world may believe; Mary at Fatima calls us to the prayer that makes that unity possible.
2027-05-13.resolve: Pray a decade of the Rosary each day until Pentecost for peace and for the unity of Christians.

intro: Theme: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”
St Matthias, the quiet disciple chosen to complete the Twelve as a witness of the resurrection.

sub: An empty place among the Twelve.
Twelve for the tribes of Israel.
Seen with Jesus, seen him risen.
q: You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
So one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us … one of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection.
points.apply: This week, tell one person in simple words what the risen Jesus means to you.

q: For the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Then they prayed and said, “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen
points.apply: Before every important decision this week, stop and pray: Lord, you know the heart; show me what you have chosen.

q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last,
points.apply: Each morning this week, thank Jesus for choosing you, and ask what fruit he wants from you that day.

points.h: From the dust to the princes
q: He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes, with the princes of his people.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
points.apply: Thank someone in your parish whose service usually goes unnoticed.

concl: Matthias was chosen not for fame or gifts but because he had stayed with Jesus and seen him risen.
The Lord who chose him chooses us as friends, and sends us to bear fruit that will last.
2027-05-14.resolve: Pray before your next important decision, and tell someone this week why you believe that Jesus is risen.

intro: Theme: “What is that to you? Follow me!”
